sections.title: Relay
sections.heading: Relay
sections.text:
One API for AI inference: chat, images, video, audio, embeddings, multi-model
workflows and rentable machines, all on one key and one credit balance.

Relay exposes standard REST endpoints, OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible where
those formats exist, and handles provider selection, load balancing and
failover for you.

sections.title: Relay
sections.heading: Three things to know first
sections.text:
- **`mode` is a request-body field**, not a header or query parameter. Leave it
  out (it defaults to `auto`) unless you need a specific mode; see [Modes](./reference/modes.md).
- **Video is asynchronous by default.** A video request returns a `task_id`;
  poll `GET /v2/tasks/{task_id}` or register a webhook. See
  [Tasks & Webhooks](./reference/async-webhooks.md).
- **Polling a task needs no auth header.** The `task_id` is the access token,
  so treat it like a secret.

sections.title: Relay
sections.heading: How it works
sections.text:
Relay names every model it serves as **mode.source.model**:

```
mode       → where it runs and how it is billed: direct or opengpu (auto picks for you)
source     → the API family: openai, anthropic, image, video, audio, embedding
model      → the model ID you send, e.g. openai/gpt-5.4 or anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
```

**Modes:**
- `direct`: low-latency (<1s) execution on managed GPU providers
- `opengpu`: decentralized execution on the [OpenGPU Network](https://opengpu.network), a permissionless compute network with redundant computing and on-chain settlement

This three-part name is also what tier restrictions, key allowlists and usage
reports use.

sections.title: Relay
sections.heading: Quick example
sections.text:
```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "openai/gpt-5.4", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}'
```

sections.title: Audio
sections.heading: Audio
sections.text:
Text-to-speech (TTS) and speech-to-text (STT). Each TTS model has its own
route under `/v2/audio/...`; all transcription models share
`/v2/audio/asr/whisper`. Call them with an API key or as a guest on
guest-enabled models. The exact routes, voices and per-model parameters are
listed in the [API Explorer → Audio](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer).

Requests are synchronous by default (both directions are fast); set
`"async": true` to get a `task_id` to poll for longer inputs.

| Route | Model | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v2/audio/index-tts-2/generate` | IndexTTS-2 | audio inline (base64) |
| `POST /v2/audio/minimax-speech-2-8-hd/generate` | MiniMax speech-2.8-hd | audio inline (base64) |
| `POST /v2/audio/qwen3-tts-flash/generate` | Qwen3-TTS-Flash | a link to the audio |
| `POST /v2/audio/asr/whisper` | transcription models (below) | text |

The TTS routes do not share a body: IndexTTS-2 and Qwen3-TTS-Flash take
`input` (Qwen3-TTS-Flash also requires a `voice`), MiniMax takes `text` and
requires a `voice_id`. Check
each route in the API Explorer.

sections.title: Audio
sections.heading: Text to speech
sections.text:
```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/audio/index-tts-2/generate \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": "Hello from Relay"}'
```

The response shape depends on the model; there are two shapes.

Qwen `qwen3-tts-flash` returns a **link**:
`{"audio_url": "https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/0jTz5Ht994t1szRMSgF1JQ",
"characters": 52, "audio_id": "...", "task_id": "...", "mode": "direct"}`.

`index-tts-2` (shown above) and MiniMax `speech-2.8-hd` return the audio
**inline**, base64-encoded — decode it and write the bytes to a file:
`{"audio_base64": "UklGRiQAAABXQVZFZm10...", "content_type": "audio/wav",
"task_id": "...", "mode": "direct"}` (MiniMax also reports `audio_length_ms`,
`audio_format`, `audio_size_bytes`, `audio_sample_rate` and `audio_channel`).

Hosted `audio_url` links live **1 hour** by default, alongside the task record.
Add `store_output: relay1d`, `relay7d` or `relay30d` to keep both for 1, 7 or 30
days for a flat per-file fee — see [Video → How long the link lives](video.md)
and `media_storage` in `GET /v2/pricing`. `store_output` is **not available on
the inline routes above**: there is no link to host, so a `relay*` value returns
`422` naming the model. `store_output_supported` in `GET /v2/models` is the
authoritative per-model answer.

IndexTTS-2's voice-cloning reference `spk_audio_url` takes a URL or base64, but
its emotion reference `emo_audio_url` is a URL only. Local file? Upload it with
[Files](files.md) and pass the returned `url`.

sections.title: Audio
sections.heading: Speech to text
sections.text:
The transcription models share one endpoint; `model` is **required** and
picks between them.

| `model` | Billed | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `openai/whisper-1` | per second of audio | `text`, `language`, `duration` |
| `openai/gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` | per token | `text` |
| `openai/whisper-large-v3` | — | **currently unavailable** (`403 MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE`); the name stays accepted so it can return |

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/audio/asr/whisper \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "openai/whisper-1",
       "audio_url": "https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/NyBogi-5y4X2Mo0XHfGbHQ"}'
```

```json
{
  "text": "The great brown fox jumps over the lazy dog near the riverbank.",
  "language": "english",
  "duration": 3.2,
  "task_id": "direct:...",
  "mode": "direct"
}
```

`audio_url` is a URL only — there is no base64 form. Local file? Upload it with
[Files](files.md) and pass the returned `url`.

`gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` returns `text` alone — it reports neither the language
nor the clip's length.

`language` (an ISO 639-1 hint) and `temperature` apply to every model.
`prompt` — a style hint, or the previous segment to continue from — is a
`whisper-1` and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` option; `task: "translate"`,
`return_timestamps`, `chunk_length_s` and `batch_size` belong to `whisper-large-v3`
only, and are refused while it is unavailable. Sending one to a model that does not take it returns `422` naming the
model, so nothing is ever silently dropped.

The transcript comes back as text, so there is no media link to host and
`store_output` is not part of this request.

For full parameter details per model, see the [API Explorer → Audio](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer).

sections.title: Chat
sections.heading: Chat
sections.text:
Two chat endpoints, one per API format: an OpenAI-compatible one and an
Anthropic-compatible one, each with its own model catalog. Call them with an
API key (either header), your dashboard login, or as a guest on
guest-enabled models. Point the official OpenAI or Anthropic SDK at Relay and
it works unchanged. The live model list is [`GET /v2/models`](models.md).

| Source | Endpoint | Format | Streaming |
|--------|----------|--------|-----------|
| OpenAI | `POST /v2/openai/v1/chat/completions` | OpenAI-compatible | Yes |
| Anthropic | `POST /v2/anthropic/v1/messages` | Anthropic-compatible | Yes |

sections.title: Chat
sections.heading: Examples
sections.text:
**OpenAI-compatible:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "openai/gpt-5.4", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}'
```

Or with the OpenAI SDK, pointing `base_url` at the Relay OpenAI path:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://relaygpu.com/v2/openai/v1", api_key="YOUR_KEY")
resp = client.chat.completions.create(model="openai/gpt-5.4", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}])
```

The Anthropic path works the same way with the Anthropic SDK: set its `base_url` to `https://relaygpu.com/v2/anthropic` (the SDK appends `/v1/messages`).

**Anthropic:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/anthropic/v1/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}], "max_tokens": 1024}'
```

All chat endpoints support `"async": true` for asynchronous execution; see
[Tasks & Webhooks](../reference/async-webhooks.md).

sections.title: Chat
sections.heading: Streaming
sections.text:
OpenAI and Anthropic endpoints support real-time streaming via Server-Sent Events (SSE). Add `"stream": true` to your request body. Streaming is direct mode only and cannot be combined with `async`.

**OpenAI** (standard OpenAI SSE format):

```bash
curl -N -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "openai/gpt-5.4", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}], "stream": true}'
```

Each chunk is a `data:` line containing a JSON object, terminated by a blank line:

```
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello"},"index":0}]}

data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"delta":{"content":" there"},"index":0}]}

data: [DONE]
```

**Anthropic** (Anthropic SSE format with `event:` + `data:` pairs):

```bash
curl -N -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/anthropic/v1/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}], "max_tokens": 1024, "stream": true}'
```

Events follow the Anthropic Messages API streaming format:

```
event: message_start
data: {"type":"message_start","message":{"id":"msg_...","model":"claude-sonnet-4-6","role":"assistant"}}

event: content_block_delta
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":0,"delta":{"type":"text_delta","text":"Hello"}}

event: content_block_delta
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":0,"delta":{"type":"text_delta","text":" there"}}

event: message_stop
data: {"type":"message_stop"}
```

**Notes:**
- Use `curl -N` (or disable buffering in your HTTP client) to receive chunks in real time
- Response content type is `text/event-stream`

sections.title: Chat
sections.heading: Prompt caching (Anthropic)
sections.text:
The Anthropic endpoint supports Anthropic's prompt caching. Mark the end of a
long, reused prefix with `cache_control`; a later request that repeats the
prefix within the TTL reads it back at the cache-read rate instead of paying
full input price.

**Where markers go** — the same places Anthropic takes them:

| Where | Example |
|---|---|
| `system` blocks | `"system": [{"type": "text", "text": "…", "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}]` |
| `messages[].content` blocks (text, image, document, `tool_use`, `tool_result`) | `{"type": "text", "text": "…", "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}` |
| `tools` entries | `{"name": "…", "input_schema": {…}, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}` |
| top level (automatic caching) | `"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}` |

A marker is exactly `{"type": "ephemeral"}` with an optional `"ttl"`: `"5m"`
(the default) or `"1h"`. Anything else — another `type`, another `ttl`, an
extra key — is a `422`. At most 4 markers per request (Anthropic's limit).

**Automatic caching.** A top-level `cache_control` puts the breakpoint on the
last cacheable block for you: the last block of the last message (walking back
past thinking blocks and empty text, then through `system`, then `tools`). If
nothing is cacheable, the request runs uncached. It is a `400` when your own
markers already use all 4 slots, or when that last block carries its own marker
with a different `ttl` (the same `ttl` is fine).

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/anthropic/v1/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5", "max_tokens": 1024,
       "system": [{"type": "text", "text": "<long reference document>",
                   "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"}}],
       "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarise section 2."}]}'
```

**Price per class.** Every prompt token is billed at the rate of its class:
fresh input at `per_1m_input_tokens`, cache reads at
`per_1m_cached_input_tokens`, 5-minute writes at
`per_1m_cache_write_5m_input_tokens`, 1-hour writes at
`per_1m_cache_write_1h_input_tokens` — all listed per model on
[`GET /v2/pricing`](https://relaygpu.com/v2/pricing). A model caches only when
its pricing lists the read rate and both write rates; on any other model a
request carrying `cache_control` is a `422` naming the model.

**Usage.** The response's `usage` is Anthropic's, returned verbatim:
`input_tokens` (the uncached remainder), `cache_creation_input_tokens`,
`cache_read_input_tokens` and the per-TTL `cache_creation` breakdown. Below the
model's minimum cacheable length Anthropic reports a write of `0` and the
request bills as uncached.

**Isolation.** Caches are private to your account: when a request carries a
marker, Relay prepends a short namespace block to `system` (tool-definition
markers move onto it, keeping the longest `ttl`). Its few tokens are part of the
cached prefix and are billed with it. All keys of one account share the
account's caches.

**Getting reads.** Reads land best on repeated requests with a byte-identical
prefix within the TTL; Relay sends an account's cached requests for a model
back to where the cache was written while that is available.

**Guests** cannot use prompt caching (`422`) — authenticate with an API key.

For full parameter details, available models, and response schemas, see the [API Explorer](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer).

sections.title: Chat
sections.heading: Changes
sections.text:
- **2026-09-24** — prompt caching on the Anthropic endpoint. `cache_control` is
  accepted wherever Anthropic takes it (including top-level automatic caching)
  instead of being refused with `422`; reads and 5-minute / 1-hour writes are
  billed at their own rates on models whose pricing lists them.

sections.title: Embeddings
sections.heading: Embeddings
sections.text:
Generate vector embeddings from text. The endpoint is **OpenAI-compatible** (a
drop-in for the OpenAI SDK's embeddings API), served under
`/v2/openai/v1/embeddings`. The available models and per-model parameters are listed
in the [API Explorer → Embeddings](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer),
the single source of truth, always in sync with what's live.

Call it with an API key or as a guest on guest-enabled models. Requests are
synchronous (embedding is fast) and run in direct mode. `input` accepts a single
string or a list of strings (batch), or pre-tokenized IDs; the response returns
one vector per input, in order.

sections.title: Embeddings
sections.heading: Example
sections.text:
```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/openai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "openai/text-embedding-3-small", "input": "The quick brown fox"}'
```

Or with the OpenAI SDK, pointing `base_url` at the Relay OpenAI path:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://relaygpu.com/v2/openai/v1", api_key="YOUR_KEY")
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="openai/text-embedding-3-small", input="The quick brown fox")
```

The response follows the OpenAI embeddings shape: `{object, data: [{embedding, index}], model, usage}`.
Billing is per **input** token only (embeddings produce no output tokens).

For full parameter details per model, see the [API Explorer → Embeddings](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer).

sections.title: Files
sections.heading: Files
sections.text:
Host a file from your own machine and get back a link that any `*_url` request
field accepts — `video_url`, `audio_url`, `reference_video_url`, an image URL
field, and so on. Upload once, then pass the link to as many requests as you
like while it lives.

Many routes take a source video or audio file **only** as a URL (see
[Video](video.md#source-video-and-audio-inputs) and [Audio](audio.md)). If the
file is on your disk, upload it here first.

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /v2/files` | Upload a file — the raw bytes, or a public URL to copy |
| `GET /v2/files/{file_id}` | One file: its link, status and time left |
| `GET /v2/files` | Your files, newest first — uploads **and** hosted results |
| `DELETE /v2/files/{file_id}` | Take the link down now |

All four take your API key (`X-API-Key: relay_sk_...` or
`Authorization: Bearer relay_sk_...`). Guests cannot host files: a call without
a credential returns `403 TIER_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE`.

sections.title: Files
sections.heading: Upload a file
sections.text:
Two forms share one route. Pick by `Content-Type`.

**Raw bytes** — the file is the request body, and its `Content-Type` must be an
image, video or audio type. `retention` and `filename` go on the query string:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://relaygpu.com/v2/files?retention=relay1d&filename=clip.mp4" \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: video/mp4" \
  --data-binary @clip.mp4
```

**A public URL** — send JSON and Relay copies the object for you. `retention`
and `filename` go in the body:

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/files \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://example.com/voice.wav", "retention": "relay1h"}'
```

Both answer `201` with the file:

```json
{
  "file_id": "file_3f9c2a7d1e0b4c58a6d2e9f1",
  "url": "https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/0jTz5Ht994t1szRMSgF1JQ",
  "source": "upload",
  "content_type": "video/mp4",
  "size_bytes": 18734211,
  "retention": "relay1d",
  "expires_at": "2026-10-06T09:14:02Z",
  "seconds_left": 86400,
  "cost_usd": 0.0005,
  "created_at": "2026-10-05T09:14:02Z",
  "status": "ready",
  "task_id": null,
  "workflow_run_id": null,
  "used_by": []
}
```

Pass `url` straight into a request:

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/video/bria-upscale/generate \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"video_url": "https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/0jTz5Ht994t1szRMSgF1JQ"}'
```

sections.title: Files
sections.heading: Retention
sections.text:
`retention` decides how long the link lives. Choose it at upload time: it
**cannot be extended** afterwards. If you need the file for longer, upload it
again with a longer retention.

| `retention` | Link lives | Fee |
|---|---|---|
| `relay1h` (default) | 1 hour | Free — counts against your daily free upload quota |
| `relay1d` | 1 day | Per-file fee |
| `relay7d` | 7 days | Per-file fee |
| `relay30d` | 30 days | Per-file fee |

The per-file fees are the same `media_storage` fees that `store_output` uses on
results — current rates, and which options are offered right now, are in
[`GET /v2/pricing`](models.md#output-media-storage-fees). An option missing
from that block returns `422`. The fee is charged once the file is stored; if
the upload fails, nothing is charged.

sections.title: Files
sections.heading: Limits
sections.text:
- **100 MB per file**, on both forms. A larger file returns `413 FILE_TOO_LARGE`.
- **Images, video and audio only.** Anything else returns
  `415 FILE_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` — for the URL form, that is judged on the object
  Relay fetched.
- **Daily free quota.** `relay1h` uploads count against a daily quota of files
  and bytes, set per tier. Once it is used up, free uploads return
  `429 FILE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` with a `Retry-After` header counting to the next
  00:00 UTC, when the quota resets. Paid retention (`relay1d`, `relay7d`,
  `relay30d`) is **not** limited by this quota.
- Uploads also count against your tier's per-minute rate limit
  (`429 RATE_LIMITED`; see [Rate Limits](../reference/rate-limits.md)).

sections.title: Files
sections.heading: Safe retries
sections.text:
Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (any string up to 255 characters, unique per
file) to make a retry safe: a repeat of the same upload answers with the same
`file_id` and is not charged again.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://relaygpu.com/v2/files?retention=relay7d" \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..." \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: clip-2026-10-05-001" \
  -H "Content-Type: video/mp4" \
  --data-binary @clip.mp4
```

sections.title: Files
sections.heading: Read a file
sections.text:
```bash
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/files/file_3f9c2a7d1e0b4c58a6d2e9f1 \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..."
```

Returns the same object as the upload. The fields to watch:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `status` | `ready` (the link works), `expired` (its retention ran out) or `deleted` (you took it down) |
| `seconds_left` | Time until `expires_at`; `0` unless `status` is `ready` |
| `used_by` | The last 20 task ids whose request referenced this link |
| `source` | `upload` (you uploaded it) or `result` (a model produced it) |
| `cost_usd` | The fee charged for an upload; `null` on results, which are billed on their task |
| `task_id`, `workflow_run_id` | On a result: the task (and workflow run) that produced it |

An expired file stays readable for 24 hours after it expires. After that — or
for an id that is not yours — the answer is `404 FILE_NOT_FOUND`.

sections.title: Files
sections.heading: List your files
sections.text:
```bash
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/files?source=upload&limit=20" \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..."
```

```json
{
  "files": [
    {"file_id": "file_3f9c2a7d1e0b4c58a6d2e9f1", "url": "https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/0jTz5Ht994t1szRMSgF1JQ",
     "source": "upload", "content_type": "video/mp4", "size_bytes": 18734211, "retention": "relay1d",
     "expires_at": "2026-10-06T09:14:02Z", "seconds_left": 86213, "cost_usd": 0.0005,
     "created_at": "2026-10-05T09:14:02Z", "status": "ready", "task_id": null,
     "workflow_run_id": null, "used_by": ["direct:7b1e0c4a-..."]}
  ],
  "next_cursor": "file_3f9c2a7d1e0b4c58a6d2e9f1"
}
```

The list holds your uploads **and** the media results Relay hosted for your
requests (`source: "result"`, with the `task_id` that produced them, and
`retention` set to the `store_output` option the request used, or `relay1h` for
the default hour). Newest first; deleted files and files expired more than 24
hours ago are left out.

| Query | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `source` | `upload` or `result`; omit for both |
| `status` | `ready` or `expired`; omit for both |
| `limit` | 1–200, default 50 |
| `cursor` | The previous page's `next_cursor`; `next_cursor` is `null` on the last page |

sections.title: Files
sections.heading: Delete a file
sections.text:
```bash
curl -X DELETE https://relaygpu.com/v2/files/file_3f9c2a7d1e0b4c58a6d2e9f1 \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..."
```

Answers `204` with no body. The link stops working from the next request, and
the file reads back with `status: "deleted"`. Deleting is idempotent: deleting
it again also answers `204`. Deleting a result leaves its task untouched. No fee
is refunded.

sections.title: Files
sections.heading: Errors
sections.text:
Every error carries the usual envelope (see [Errors](../reference/errors.md)).

| Status | `error.code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| `402` | `INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS` | A paid retention and your balance is below the credit floor |
| `402` | `KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` | This sub-key's `key_budget` is used up |
| `403` | `TIER_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE` | No credential — guests cannot host files |
| `404` | `FILE_NOT_FOUND` | Unknown id, another account's file, or expired more than 24 hours ago |
| `413` | `FILE_TOO_LARGE` | The file is larger than 100 MB |
| `415` | `FILE_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` | Not an image, video or audio file |
| `422` | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Bad `retention`, `url` or `filename`, an empty body, a retention not offered right now, or an unknown `cursor` |
| `429` | `FILE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` | The daily free (`relay1h`) quota is used up — `Retry-After` counts to 00:00 UTC |
| `429` | `RATE_LIMITED` | The per-minute rate limit — `Retry-After` is set |
| `502` | `UPSTREAM_ERROR` | The file could not be stored, the URL could not be fetched, or a delete could not take the link down — retry later |

For full request and response schemas, see the
[API Explorer → Files](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer).

sections.title: Images
sections.heading: Images
sections.text:
Generate images from text prompts, or edit existing ones. Each model family has
its own route. Call them with an API key or as a guest on guest-enabled models.
Requests are synchronous by default; add `"async": true` for a `task_id`.

The one thing to know: **some routes return the image inline as base64, others
return a link** that expires after 1 hour unless you store it. Each section
below says which.

sections.title: Images
sections.heading: Available endpoints
sections.text:
| Model family | Endpoint | Type |
|----------|----------|------|
| Flux 2 Pro | `POST /v2/image/flux/generate` | Text-to-image |
| Gemini 3 Pro / 3.1 Flash / 2.5 Flash | `POST /v2/image/gemini-3/generate` | Text-to-image / editing (multi-image on 3 Pro) |
| GPT Image 1.5 | `POST /v2/image/gpt-image/generate` | Text-to-image |
| GPT Image 1.5 | `POST /v2/image/gpt-image/edit` | Image-to-image |
| GPT Image 2 / 2.5 Sunburst / 2.5 Flare | `POST /v2/image/gpt-image-2/generate` | Text-to-image / editing / multi-image composition |
| Qwen | `POST /v2/image/qwen/generate` | Text-to-image |
| Qwen | `POST /v2/image/qwen/edit` | Image-to-image |
| Seedream 5.0 Pro | `POST /v2/image/seedream-5-0-pro/generate` | Text-to-image / editing (up to 14 references) |
| Wan 2.7 Image Pro | `POST /v2/image/wan-2-7-image-pro/generate` | Text-to-image / editing / multi-image fusion |
| Real-ESRGAN | `POST /v2/image/realesrgan/upscale` | Upscaling (2x / 4x) — **currently unavailable** |
| FLUX.2 klein | `POST /v2/image/flux-1/generate` | Text-to-image — **currently unavailable** (`403 MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE`); use `/v2/image/flux/generate` |

The `model` you see in `GET /v2/models` maps to its family route above. Send
each model to its own route: the routes are not interchangeable, and a model
sent to another family's route is not supported.

**Prompt length.** The GPT Image routes accept up to **32,000** characters,
OpenAI's documented maximum for those models. No other image model has a limit
of ours: send the prompt you need, and if it is too long for the provider, the
provider's own refusal comes back to you as a `400`.

sections.title: Images
sections.heading: Example
sections.text:
```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/image/flux/generate \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "A red fox in autumn forest", "width": 1024, "height": 1024}'
```

Result shape depends on the model family. **FLUX, GPT Image, and Gemini** return
base64-encoded images (PNG unless you set `output_format`) in an `images`
array; decode each string to get the bytes:

```json
{
  "images": ["<base64-encoded PNG>", "..."]
}
```

**Gemini** additionally returns `finish_reason` — the model's own completion
verdict, forwarded verbatim from upstream. `"STOP"` is a normal generation; the
field is null when upstream reported none, and it is absent on every non-Gemini
image model. Token counts are deliberately not returned: these models bill
per image, not per token.

```json
{
  "images": ["<base64-encoded PNG>"],
  "finish_reason": "STOP"
}
```

When a request produces no image at all, that verdict comes back under
`error.detail` instead, alongside `block_reason` and any reply the model wrote
in words — see [Errors](../reference/errors.md#error-codes) for
`CONTENT_POLICY_DECLINED`, `IMAGE_TEXT_RESPONSE` and `IMAGE_NO_OUTPUT`. Note
that `finish_reason: "STOP"` on its own does not mean an image was produced.

**Qwen, Seedream and Wan2.7** instead return Relay-hosted image URLs in a `urls` array:

```json
{
  "urls": ["https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/0jTz5Ht994t1szRMSgF1JQ", "..."]
}
```

Those links live **1 hour** by default, alongside the task record. Add
`store_output: relay1d`, `relay7d` or `relay30d` to keep both for 1, 7 or 30
days for a flat per-file fee — see [Video → How long the link lives](video.md)
and `media_storage` in `GET /v2/pricing`.

`store_output` is **not available on the base64 routes above** (gemini,
gpt-image, FLUX, upscalers): there is no link to host, so a `relay*` value
returns `422` naming the model. Which models offer it is published per model as
`store_output_supported` in `GET /v2/models`, so you can check before you send.
The default `provider` is accepted everywhere.

sections.title: Images
sections.heading: Multi-image editing (Gemini 3 Pro)
sections.text:
`google/gemini-3-pro-image` can take up to **14** reference images in one
request and edit across them — compositing, colour-matching, style transfer
between sources. Pass them as `images` instead of the single `image` field:

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/image/gemini-3/generate \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "google/gemini-3-pro-image",
       "prompt": "Repaint the blue wall in the first image using the exact orange colour of the second image. Keep everything else identical.",
       "images": ["<base64 PNG>", "<base64 PNG>"],
       "image_size": "1K"}'
```

Rules:

- `image` and `images` are **mutually exclusive** — sending both is a `422`.
- `images` accepts **1-14** items; outside that range is a `422`.
- Each item is raw base64 or a data URI (`data:image/png;base64,...`), same
  encoding as `image`.
- **Gemini 3 Pro only.** `gemini-2.5-flash-image` and
  `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview` take a single `image`; sending `images` to
  either is a `422`.
- Prompt ordering matters — refer to sources positionally ("the first image",
  "the second image").

Billing is per output resolution tier, unchanged by the number of references.

sections.title: Images
sections.heading: GPT Image 2 and 2.5
sections.text:
Three models on one route; `model` picks between them and defaults to
`openai/gpt-image-2`. The body is identical for all three — `prompt` alone for
text-to-image, plus a base64 `image` (and optional `mask`) to edit, or a list of
base64 `image`s to compose.

| `model` | Billed |
|---|---|
| `openai/gpt-image-2` | per image, at the requested `size` |
| `openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` | per token |
| `openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare` | per token |

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/image/gpt-image-2/generate \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst",
       "prompt": "A single green pear on a wooden table, soft window light",
       "size": "1536x1024"}'
```

On the 2.5 variants `size` asks for a resolution; it does not set the price.
What you pay follows the input and output tokens the model reports, at the rates
in `GET /v2/pricing` — so a larger `size` costs more only insofar as it takes
more output tokens to draw, and `n` multiplies the bill the same way it does
everywhere.

All three return their images inline as base64, so `store_output` has nothing to
host — `relay1d`/`relay7d`/`relay30d` return `422`.

sections.title: Images
sections.heading: Seedream 5.0 Pro
sections.text:
ByteDance's flagship image model: text-to-image, and editing or composition
from up to 14 reference pictures. Unlike the other image routes it returns
**links**, not inline base64 — so `store_output` genuinely applies here (see
[the note above](#example)).

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/image/seedream-5-0-pro/generate \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "A watercolor fox sitting under a maple tree, autumn colors",
       "size": "2048x2048"}'
```

```json
{
  "urls": ["https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/..."],
  "model": "ByteDance/doubao-seedream-5-0-pro-260628",
  "size": "2048x2048"
}
```

sections.title: Images
sections.heading: Sizing and what it costs
sections.text:
`size` takes either a preset or exact pixels:

| Value | Meaning | Bills at |
|---|---|---|
| `1K` | ~1.0MP, aspect chosen from the prompt | `1K` rate |
| `2K` | ~4.2MP, aspect chosen from the prompt | `2K` rate |
| `<width>x<height>` | exact, e.g. `1920x1080` | `1K` at or below 1024x1024 in **total area**, `2K` above |

The default is `2048x2048`. Total area must not exceed 4,624,220 pixels
(~4.6MP) — the published 4K tier is not available on the pro variant, and a
larger request is a `422` naming the size. Rates are on `/v2/pricing`.

sections.title: Images
sections.heading: References
sections.text:
Pass 1-14 pictures in `images`, each an https URL or a data URI:

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/image/seedream-5-0-pro/generate \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "Repaint the wall in the first image using the exact colour of the second image. Keep everything else identical.",
       "images": ["https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/Usw6wp8ht34vuLTPh6XHWA",
                  "https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/fZqlx8XpM0z1nwLfHL9rhQ"],
       "size": "2K"}'
```

Refer to sources positionally in the prompt ("the first image"). Billing is per
output resolution tier, unchanged by the number of references.

`watermark` (default `false`) adds the upstream's AI-generated mark;
`output_format` is `jpeg` (default) or `png`.

sections.title: Images
sections.heading: Wan 2.7 Image Pro
sections.text:
Alibaba's Wan2.7: text-to-image, editing, and fusing several pictures into one.
Like Seedream it returns **links** rather than inline base64, so `store_output`
applies here.

One route covers three jobs, chosen by what you send — at least one of
`prompt`, `image` or `images` is required:

| You send | You get |
|---|---|
| `prompt` | text-to-image |
| `prompt` + `image` | that one picture, edited |
| `prompt` + `images` | several pictures fused or edited together |

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/image/wan-2-7-image-pro/generate \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "A lighthouse on a rocky coast at dusk, warm lamplight, painterly style",
       "size": "1K"}'
```

```json
{
  "urls": ["https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/..."],
  "model": "Wan-AI/Wan2.7-Image-Pro",
  "size": "1K"
}
```

sections.title: Images
sections.heading: Sizing and what it costs
sections.text:
`size` takes the preset `1K`, `2K` or `4K`, or exact pixels as `2048x2048`.
Omit it and the upstream picks. **The price is the same at every size** — so
unlike Seedream, sizing here is purely a quality choice.

What *does* change the price is `n`: **every image returned is billed**, so
`n: 4` costs four times `n: 1` — and if you also pass `store_output`, four
storage fees with it. `n` is 1–4 normally; `enable_sequential` raises the cap
to 16 for generating a related series rather than variations. Above those
bounds the request is a `422` rather than a surprise on your bill.

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/image/wan-2-7-image-pro/generate \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "Place the subject of the first image into the setting of the second, matching the light",
       "images": ["https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/Usw6wp8ht34vuLTPh6XHWA",
                  "https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/fZqlx8XpM0z1nwLfHL9rhQ"],
       "size": "2K"}'
```

Refer to sources positionally in the prompt ("the first image"). `seed` makes a
result reproducible, `watermark` (default `false`) adds the upstream's
AI-generated mark, and `thinking_mode` trades speed for a more considered
composition.

sections.title: Images
sections.heading: Upscaling
sections.text:
**Currently unavailable: no Real-ESRGAN model is being served right now, and
every request returns `403 MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE`.** The contract below stays as
documented and works as-is once a provider returns.

Real-ESRGAN raises the resolution of an existing image. There is no prompt —
the output is the input multiplied by the model's fixed scale factor:

| Model | Scale | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| `TencentARC/RealESRGAN-x4plus` | 4x | photographic (default) |
| `TencentARC/RealESRGAN-x2plus` | 2x | thumbnails, bulk catalog work |
| `TencentARC/RealESRGAN-x4plus-anime` | 4x | anime and illustration |

Pass exactly one of `image_url` or `image_b64`. Limits: 20MB input file,
16MP input pixels. `output_format` accepts `png` (default), `jpeg`, `jpg` or
`webp` — the alpha channel survives `png` and `webp` only.

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/image/realesrgan/upscale \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"image_url": "https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/Usw6wp8ht34vuLTPh6XHWA",
       "model": "TencentARC/RealESRGAN-x2plus"}'
```

Returns the upscaled image base64-encoded in `images`, alongside the output
geometry:

```json
{
  "images": ["<base64-encoded PNG>"],
  "model": "TencentARC/RealESRGAN-x4plus",
  "width": 2048,
  "height": 2048,
  "scale": 4
}
```

All image endpoints support `"async": true` for longer generations, with
optional [webhook delivery](../reference/async-webhooks.md) on completion.

For full parameter details per provider, see the [API Explorer → Image](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer).

sections.title: Images
sections.heading: Changes
sections.text:
- **2026-09-22** — prompt limits are the vendor's or there are none. The GPT
  Image routes rose from 4,000 to OpenAI's documented **32,000** characters;
  Gemini, Qwen, Seedream, Wan 2.7 Image Pro and FLUX lost their
  4,000-character cap entirely. Nothing got stricter: every prompt that worked
  before still works, and longer ones now reach the provider instead of being
  refused here.

sections.title: Instances
sections.heading: Instances
sections.text:
Rent a machine — a GPU box, an NPU container or a plain CPU server — on the same
key and the same wallet you use for inference. You pick a row from the catalog,
hand us **your** SSH public key, and the instance opens to that key alone. We
never generate or hold a private key.

Instances are a partner feature: a key on a tier that is not enabled for them
gets `403 TIER_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE`. Talk to us if you want it on your account.

sections.title: Instances
sections.heading: 1. Read the catalog
sections.text:
```bash
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/instances/catalog -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..."
```

Each row is one rentable thing — the `prescription` is the **whole** hardware
choice, so there is nothing to tune:

```json
{
  "prescription": "t4-intel-any-8vcpu-32gb-300gb",
  "service_mode": "dedicated_machine",
  "kind": "gpu",
  "description": "1× NVIDIA T4, 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM, 300 GB disk · dedicated machine",
  "cpu": {"model": "Intel Xeon", "vcpu": 8},
  "ram_gb": 32,
  "gpu": {"model": "NVIDIA T4", "count": 1, "memory_gb": 16},
  "disk_gb": 300,
  "regions": ["singapore"],
  "default_region": "singapore",
  "compatible_images": ["ubuntu-gpu"],
  "ssh_key_types": ["ssh-ed25519", "ssh-rsa", "ecdsa-sha2-nistp256"],
  "lifetime": null,
  "billing_modes": [
    {"mode": "hourly", "period_seconds": 3600, "term_seconds": null,
     "rate_per_period": 0.45, "default": true}
  ],
  "is_override": false,
  "last_spawn": {"outcome": "ready", "at": "2026-09-16T08:12:44Z", "reason": null},
  "availability": {"state": "available", "count": null, "checked_at": "2026-09-17T09:00:12Z"}
}
```

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `service_mode` | `dedicated_machine` (a VM: SSH to a public IP) or `managed_container` (SSH to a hostname and port) |
| `kind` | `gpu`, `npu` or `cpu` — what the hardware block carries |
| `default_region` | Where a request lands when it omits `region`; `null` means the platform picks |
| `ssh_key_types` | The OpenSSH key types this row accepts as `ssh_public_key` |
| `lifetime` | `{default_hours, max_hours}` where the row caps how long an instance may live; `null` = it lives until you end it |
| `rate_per_period` | **Your** price per period — a per-customer rate is already applied (`is_override`) |
| `last_spawn` | How the last attempt on this row went, across all customers: `ready`, `failed` (with the `reason` that customer was given) or `none` |
| `availability` | Whether the row can be delivered right now — see below |

Only rows you can actually rent are listed. `GET /v2/instances/images` describes
the images in `compatible_images`.

sections.title: Instances
sections.heading: Images
sections.text:
A row may list several images in `compatible_images`; the **first is the default** —
the one to pick when you have no preference. `image` is required on every
request: send the one you want, spelled exactly as the row lists it. An image
the row does not list is refused (`422`, `field: image`).
`GET /v2/instances/images` lists only images some row you can rent launches
with: what each one is, its OS, and what it has installed.

An image is software on the machine, not a service we run for you: nothing
about it is tunable on the request, and it never changes the price. Where an
image carries an app — Jupyter, ComfyUI, vLLM — you reach it over an SSH tunnel
with your own key, and you start it yourself unless the image's description
says it starts at boot. For an app listening on port 8188 of a
`dedicated_machine`:

```bash
ssh -N -L 8188:localhost:8188 root@203.0.113.10
# then open http://localhost:8188 on your own machine
```

sections.title: Instances
sections.heading: "Rentable now"
sections.text:
`availability.state` is one of three words:

- **`available`** — the supplier said it can deliver this row, in this region, at
  the moment it was asked. `count`, where a supplier states a number, is how many.
- **`sold_out`** — it said it cannot.
- **`unknown`** — nobody has an answer: the supplier exposes no capacity check,
  it did not answer in time, or capacity reporting is not live yet for this row.
  **`unknown` is not `sold_out`.** Show the row; just show no badge.

`checked_at` is when the supplier was asked. We refresh on a fixed cadence
(roughly every two minutes) and cache the answer, so reading the catalog never
waits on a supplier and never costs you a call. Two consequences worth designing
for: the state can be up to a couple of minutes old, and it is
**not a reservation** — a rent can still fail after `available`, in which case
you get the honest failure reason and nothing is billed.

sections.title: Instances
sections.heading: 2. Rent one
sections.text:
```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/instances \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prescription":"t4-intel-any-8vcpu-32gb-300gb",
       "image":"ubuntu-gpu",
       "ssh_public_key":"ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3Nza... you@laptop",
       "region":"singapore"}'
```

```json
{"id": "inst_9f3c...", "status": "requested"}
```

`202` means the request is recorded, not that the machine exists — provisioning
takes a few minutes. Optional fields: `service_mode` (required only when the
prescription is offered in more than one), `billing_mode` (defaults to the row's
default), `region` (defaults to `default_region`), `max_lifetime_hours` (only on
rows with a `lifetime`), and `webhook_url` for a signed push on
`instance.ready` / `instance.failed` / `instance.terminated`, plus
`instance.warning` (your balance fell below your warning threshold) and
`instance.grace` (a grace countdown started, where one is configured).
`prescription`, `image` and `ssh_public_key` are required.

`ssh_public_key` is one OpenSSH public-key line whose type is in the row's
`ssh_key_types`. It is the only way in: no password, no second key.

sections.title: Instances
sections.heading: 3. Poll it
sections.text:
```bash
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/instances/inst_9f3c... -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..."
```

`status` runs `requested` → `provisioning` → `ready` → `terminating` →
`terminated`, or `failed`. From `ready` the instance carries `connection`,
shaped by its `service_mode`:

```json
{"status": "ready",
 "prescription": "t4-intel-any-8vcpu-32gb-300gb",
 "display_name": "T4 · dedicated machine",
 "kind": "gpu",
 "connection": {"public_ip": "203.0.113.10", "port": 22, "user": "root"},
 "ssh_key_fingerprint": "SHA256:...",
 "expires_at": null, "rate_per_period": 0.45,
 "hours_billed": 1.0, "spend_usd": 0.45}
```

Which is `ssh root@203.0.113.10` for a `dedicated_machine`, and
`ssh -p <port> <user>@<hostname>` for a `managed_container`.

An instance also says what it **is** and what it **costs**, so a card never has
to join the catalog to draw itself:

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `display_name` | The row's name as it read when you rented it, kept on the instance — so it survives the row being retired or withdrawn. `null` on instances requested before we recorded it |
| `kind` | `gpu`, `npu` or `cpu`, likewise |
| `rate_per_period` | **Your** price for the next period this instance bills — the same number the meter charges, per-customer rate already applied. `null` when nothing prices the row any more, in which case nothing is billed either |

Every timestamp here is UTC with a trailing `Z`
(`2026-09-17T19:18:32.678686Z`).

`GET /v2/instances` lists yours, newest first. Scope it:

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| `status` | Exact statuses, comma-separated (`ready,failed`), and/or the group words `current` (requested, provisioning, ready, terminating) and `ended` (terminated, failed) |
| `limit` | Page size, 1–500; without it you get the 200 newest |
| `starting_after` | An instance id — the page continues after it. Must be one of yours, otherwise `400` |

```bash
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/instances?status=current&limit=20" -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..."
```

`count` is how many rows came back, `total` how many match the filter; when
`has_more` is true, pass `next_cursor` as `starting_after` for the next page.

```bash
# page one, then the next one
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/instances?status=ended&limit=20" -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..."
# → {"count": 20, "total": 57, "has_more": true, "next_cursor": "inst_8f3c...", ...}
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/instances?status=ended&limit=20&starting_after=inst_8f3c..." \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..."
```

Repeat until `has_more` is false, where `next_cursor` is `null`. `total` counts
the filter, not the page, so it is the same number on every page of a walk —
the cursor does not narrow it. The cursor is a *position* in the order (newest
first), not
a member of the filter: an instance that is still running is a valid
`starting_after` for `?status=ended`, and a row that ends between two of your
pages does not shift the one you ask for next.

sections.title: Instances
sections.heading: When the wallet runs out
sections.text:
While a grace countdown is running — your balance went below zero and we are
counting down to ending every instance you hold — the list carries one extra
block:

```json
{"wallet": {"balance": -0.40, "warning_threshold": 0,
            "grace_started_at": "2026-09-17T11:00:00Z",
            "grace_ends_at": "2026-09-18T11:00:00Z",
            "hours_left": 0.0}}
```

`grace_ends_at` is when that happens unless you top up. `hours_left` is
**wallet-wide**: your balance divided by the hourly cost of every instance you
hold alive, not just the rows this call returned.

Outside a countdown `wallet` is `null` — including when you are merely under
your warning threshold, where `/v2/customer/credits` already has the balance
and the threshold. A single instance (`GET /v2/instances/{id}`) never carries
it: it is a fact about your wallet, not about one machine.

When the grace window is off (`billing.grace_hours` is `0` in the catalog
response) there is no countdown to announce and none is sent: an instance simply ends at the boundary its balance could not cover, and
that boundary is its `terminate_requested_at`. When a countdown IS configured,
it ends your instances at `grace_ends_at` — the instant the window runs out,
not whenever we next look.

sections.title: Instances
sections.heading: 4. End it
sections.text:
```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/instances/inst_9f3c.../terminate \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..."
```

`202` and `status: terminating`; we execute it within about half a minute.
Billing stops at **your request**, not at the shutdown. Asking twice, or asking
about an instance that already ended, is a `200` with the current status.

Ending is available once the instance is `ready`. While it is still
`requested` or `provisioning` the call answers `409 INSTANCE_NOT_READY`:
nothing is billed before ready, and a request that never gets there fails on
its own and costs nothing.

sections.title: Instances
sections.heading: 5. What it costs
sections.text:
```bash
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/instances/usage?from=2026-09-01T00:00:00Z" \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..."
```

Per instance: billed periods, hours, your rate and spend, and when its first
and latest billed periods started (`first_period_start`, `last_period_start`),
plus totals. `totals.spend` is exactly what your wallet paid for instances.

| Term | Rule |
|---|---|
| Unit | One billing period — an hour on `hourly`; a prepaid mode charges its whole term up front |
| Starts | When the instance reaches `ready`. A request that never gets there costs nothing |
| Ends | The earliest of your terminate request, the supplier ending it, `expires_at` — and, with no grace, the start of the first period your real balance could not cover |
| Rounding | Every period that starts is charged in full. Nothing is pro-rated |
| Up front | Your real balance must cover `min_commit_hours` at the row's rate before a request is accepted, and every later period starts only if your real balance covers it — otherwise your instances end (`balance_exhausted`) and nothing is charged for the period that did not start. Promo credits never apply to instances |
| Currency | USD, from the same wallet as inference (`consumed_by_mode.instances`) |

The live numbers for `min_commit_hours` and the grace window are in the
`billing` block of the catalog response.

sections.title: Instances
sections.heading: Refusals
sections.text:
| Status | `error.code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `TIER_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE` | Your tier is not enabled for instances (a request with no key included) |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | A field the request got wrong — `error.detail.field` names it: an unknown prescription, a `service_mode` the prescription is not offered as, an incompatible `image`, a `region` the row does not have, a key type the row does not accept, an unpriced `billing_mode`, `max_lifetime_hours` on a row with no cap or outside it, or a row that **is no longer offered** |
| 402 | `INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS` | Your real balance does not cover the up-front commitment; the detail carries `required_usd` and `balance_usd`. A wallet already below its credit limit is refused earlier, with a plain message |
| 429 | `INSTANCE_LIMIT` | You already hold the maximum number of live instances |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | Too many create/terminate calls this hour; `Retry-After` is set |
| 404 | `INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND` | No instance with that id belongs to you |
| 409 | `INSTANCE_NOT_READY` | Terminate on an instance still `requested` or `provisioning`. Ending becomes available at `ready`; nothing is billed before then, and a request that never gets there costs nothing |
| 503 | `INSTANCES_UNAVAILABLE` | Instances are not available right now. When the catalog is only temporarily unreadable, `Retry-After` is set; without it, contact support |

Every refusal on the create path happens **before** anything is provisioned, so
nothing is running and nothing is billed.

A row can be retired: it leaves the catalog, and renting it answers
`422` — `'<prescription>' (<service_mode>) is no longer offered`. Instances you
already hold on a retired row keep running, and keep billing at the rate you
rented them at, until you end them.

sections.title: Instances
sections.heading: Changes
sections.text:
- **2026-09-24** — a row may list more than one image in `compatible_images`;
  the first is the default, and `image` takes the name exactly as the row
  lists it. `GET /v2/instances/images` now lists only images a row you can
  rent launches with (before, it could list an image no such row offered).
  The first such image is `comfyui` (ComfyUI, started at boot on port 8188,
  with JupyterLab installed) on the rows whose disk holds it. See
  [Images](#images).

- **2026-09-21** — `GET /v2/instances` pages. `starting_after` takes an
  instance id and continues after it; the response adds `has_more`,
  `next_cursor` and `total` (how many match the filter — `count` still means
  the rows in front of you). Nothing was removed and no default changed: a
  call that names no `starting_after` answers exactly as before.

- **2026-09-19** — a period now starts only if your real balance covers it.
  When it does not, nothing is inserted and nothing is charged for that
  period: your instances end with `balance_exhausted` instead of running an
  hour you owe for, and their `terminate_requested_at` is that boundary —
  billing ends where your balance stopped covering it. Periods already
  started are still billed in full. With the grace window off
  nothing announces a countdown any more: you get `instance.terminated` with
  `ended_reason: balance_exhausted` rather than an `instance.grace` event
  whose countdown was already over. Where a countdown IS configured, it now
  ends instances at `grace_ends_at` itself rather than at the next check, so a
  period starting in between is neither started nor billed. Also: the single
  instance view no longer carries a `wallet` key; the list still does while a
  countdown runs. Terminate is available from `ready` on: before that the
  call answers `409 INSTANCE_NOT_READY` (nothing is billed before ready).
  Usage rows carry `first_period_start` and `last_period_start`.

- **2026-09-17** — every timestamp on this surface now ends in `Z`
  (`2026-09-17T19:18:32.678686Z`); the `+00:00` spelling is gone. Instances
  carry `display_name`, `kind` and `rate_per_period`, and the list carries
  `wallet` while a grace countdown runs. Nothing was renamed or removed.

sections.title: Models & Pricing
sections.heading: Models & Pricing
sections.text:
The model list and the rates change as models are added and retired, so read
them live from these two endpoints rather than hard-coding them. Neither needs
authentication.

sections.title: Models & Pricing
sections.heading: Models
sections.text:
List every available model.

```bash
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/models
```

Returns models grouped by mode and source, plus a `model_restrictions_per_tier` map.

```json
{
  "auto": {
    "video": [
      {"name": "ByteDance/doubao-seedance-2-0-mini-260615", "tag": "text-to-video", "display_name": "Seedance 2.0 Mini", "store_output_supported": true,
       "endpoint": {"method": "POST", "path": "/v2/video/doubao-seedance-2.0-mini/generate", "operation_id": "video_doubao_seedance_2_0_mini_generate", "model_in_body": false, "model_default": null, "async_default": true, "streams": false}}
    ]
  }
}
```

**`endpoint`:** the route that serves this model, so a name is all you need to build a request. One model at a time, with its route, the request body's JSON Schema, a runnable example, what it returns, modes, list price and availability: `GET /v2/models/{model}`. Both are described in [Models](../reference/models.md).

**`store_output_supported`:** whether this model's response carries a media link
Relay can re-host, and therefore whether it accepts
[`store_output`](video.md#how-long-the-link-lives). Always present. `false` means
the model returns its media inline (base64), or has not declared the field — a
`relay1d`/`relay7d`/`relay30d` request returns `422` naming the model, while the
default `provider` still works. Under `auto` the value is what **every** mode
hosting the model offers, since `auto` may route to any of them.

**`name` vs `display_name`:** `name` is the canonical identity — send it as `model`, and scopes and billing key off it. `display_name` is the presentation string: **render it verbatim, never transform it**, and fall back to `name` when it is absent (the field is emitted only for models that have one stored). It is never accepted as an identity — a request naming a model by its display name is rejected exactly like any unknown model.

`display_name` carries NO stability contract (mutable presentation data — never key/join/cache on it). It can be re-worded at any time; `name` is the only value that is safe to store, compare or join on.

**Note:** `model_restrictions_per_tier` is a public reference matrix: the same response is returned to every caller, authenticated or not. Each row lists the `mode.source.model` scopes that tier **cannot** call; the `guest` row describes unauthenticated callers, not you. To find your own tier, call [`GET /v2/tiers`](../introduction/authentication.md#access-tiers) with your API key (`current_tier`), or `GET /v2/customer/profile` with your dashboard login, which also returns your credit balance (see [API Keys & Account](../reference/keys.md#your-profile)).

sections.title: Models & Pricing
sections.heading: Pricing
sections.text:
List pricing for all available models. No authentication required.

```bash
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/pricing
```

Returns a flat `pricing` array (one entry per mode/model), each tagged with its `billing_type` (per_token, per_image, per_second_video, ...) and only the rate fields relevant to that type.

Example response (one entry per billing type; the rates are illustrative, read the live ones from the endpoint):

```json
{
  "pricing": [
    {"mode":"direct","model":"anthropic.anthropic/claude-fable-5","billing_type":"per_token","per_1m_input_tokens":10.0,"per_1m_output_tokens":50.0,"per_1m_cached_input_tokens":1.0,"per_1m_cache_write_5m_input_tokens":12.5,"per_1m_cache_write_1h_input_tokens":20.0},
    {"mode":"direct","model":"audio.IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2","billing_type":"per_character","per_1k_characters":0.0056},
    {"mode":"direct","model":"image.Qwen/qwen-image","billing_type":"per_image","per_image":0.036},
    {"mode":"direct","model":"video.Wan-AI/Wan2.5-T2V","billing_type":"per_second_video","per_second_video":{"480p":0.05,"720p":0.1}}
  ],
  "total_count": 4
}
```

sections.title: Models & Pricing
sections.heading: Output media storage fees
sections.text:
The same response carries a `media_storage` block: the per-file fee for keeping a
media result on Relay's CDN beyond the default hour, one entry per `store_output`
option. An option **absent** from the block is not offered right now, and a request
naming it returns `422`.

```json
{
  "media_storage": {"relay1d": 0.0005, "relay7d": 0.001, "unit": "per_file"}
}
```

`unit` is `per_file`: a generation with three outputs stored for 7 days is charged
three times the `relay7d` fee, on top of the model's own price. Enterprise accounts
see their negotiated rates on `GET /v2/customer/pricing`. What the option does and
how long links live: [Video → How long the link lives](video.md#how-long-the-link-lives).

The same fees apply to files you upload yourself: a [Files](files.md) upload with
`retention: relay1d`, `relay7d` or `relay30d` is charged the matching per-file fee
from this block, exactly as a stored result is. `relay1h` uploads are free.

Rates are in USD. For full details, see the [API Explorer → Info](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer).

sections.title: Video
sections.heading: Video
sections.text:
Generate videos from text prompts (T2V), images (I2V) or other videos. Call
the routes with an API key or as a guest on guest-enabled models. Generation
takes 2–20 minutes, so **video requests are asynchronous by default**: the call
returns `202` with a `task_id` immediately, and you poll for the result (no
auth header needed) or receive a webhook. Pass `"async": false` to block and
wait for the full response instead (not recommended at these runtimes).

sections.title: Video
sections.heading: Model families
sections.text:
Several video model families are available (**Kling, Wan, Seedance, Veo,
HappyHorse, Lucy and Bria**), each with its own route(s) under `/v2/video/...`
(text-to-video, image-to-video, video-to-video, and unified generate routes,
depending on the model). The exact routes and parameters are listed in the
[API Explorer → Video](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer); the
live model list is [`GET /v2/models`](models.md). Routes the API Explorer marks
**retired** stay documented but answer `403`.

Image-conditioned models accept the reference image as a URL **or** a base64 data URI.

Video-to-video routes take a source video as well: Lucy 2.5 restyles one
(Lucy VTON 3 is retired), the Bria upscaler doubles its resolution, and
`POST /v2/video/kling-3/motion-control` transfers the motion of a person in a
reference video onto a character image.

**Prompt length.** The Kling routes accept up to **2,500** characters in
`prompt` and `negative_prompt` — Kling's own published limit. No other video
model has a limit of ours: send the prompt you need, and if it is too long for
the provider, the provider's own refusal comes back to you as a `400`.

sections.title: Video
sections.heading: Source video and audio inputs
sections.text:
A source **video or audio** file is taken by URL only — these fields do not
accept base64. Local file? Upload it with [Files](files.md) and pass the
returned `url`.

| Route | URL-only fields |
|---|---|
| `POST /v2/video/wan-25/t2v`, `/wan-25/i2v`, `/wan-26/t2v` | `audio_url` |
| Seedance 2.0 routes (`/v2/video/doubao-seedance-2.0…/generate`) | `reference_video_url`, `reference_audio_url` |
| Seedance 2.5 video-to-video (`/v2/video/doubao-seedance-2.5-v2v/generate`) | `reference_video_url`, `reference_audio_url` |
| Seedance 2.5 (`/v2/video/doubao-seedance-2.5/generate`) | `reference_audio_url` |
| `POST /v2/video/happyhorse-1.0/video-edit` | `video_url` |
| `POST /v2/video/lucy-2.5/generate` | `video_url` |
| `POST /v2/video/bria-upscale/generate` | `video_url` |
| `POST /v2/video/kling-3/motion-control` | `video_url` |
| `POST /v2/video/kling-o1/generate` | `base_video_url`, `reference_video_url` |

sections.title: Video
sections.heading: Example
sections.text:
```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/video/kling-3/t2v \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "A robot waving a flag"}'
```

**Response:**
```json
{"task_id": "direct:abc12345-...", "status": "queued", "poll_url": "/v2/tasks/direct:abc12345-..."}
```

**Poll for result** (no auth required):
```bash
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/tasks/direct:abc12345-...
```

When the task completes, the `result` (returned by the poll and the webhook) holds
Relay-hosted video URLs:
```json
{"videos": ["https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/0jTz5Ht994t1szRMSgF1JQ"]}
```
The videos are URLs; fetch them to download the generated files. Range requests
are supported, so a player can seek without downloading the whole file.

sections.title: Video
sections.heading: How long the link lives
sections.text:
By default your output link and task record live **1 hour**. Choose
`store_output: relay1d`, `relay7d` or `relay30d` and both live for the full 1, 7
or 30 days — the task stays pollable and the output stays served from Relay's
CDN — for a flat per-file fee.

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/video/wan-25/t2v \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"a red cube rotating","store_output":"relay7d"}'
```

- The fee is charged **per output file**, so a multi-output generation is
  charged per output. Current rates and the options available to you are in
  `media_storage` at [`GET /v2/pricing`](models.md) — an option missing from
  that block is not offered and returns `422`.
- After the link expires, `GET` on it returns **404**, and so does
  `GET /v2/tasks/{task_id}`. The work was still billed.
- The guest tier cannot use `store_output`; the default `provider` still returns
  a Relay-hosted link.
- Not every model offers storage: some return their media inline, with no link
  to host. `GET /v2/models` carries `store_output_supported` per model, and a
  `relay*` value on a model that says `false` returns `422` naming it. The
  default `provider` works on every model either way.
- If the storage step fails, you still get a working 1-hour link and **no fee** —
  a generation is never failed or re-billed over hosting.
- On a **synchronous** request (`"async": false`) storage runs inside the wait
  you are already holding, and gets whatever is left of it. Files stored before
  it closes keep their durable links; any still copying fall back to the 1-hour
  link, with no fee for those. Your generation is never held up or failed
  waiting on hosting. Async requests — the default for video — have no such
  ceiling, because nothing is waiting on the connection.

Prefer a push? Add a `webhook_url` to the request and we'll POST the result
to your server when it's done, signed. See
[Tasks & Webhooks](../reference/async-webhooks.md).

For full parameter details per provider, see the [API Explorer → Video](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer).

sections.title: Video
sections.heading: Changes
sections.text:
- **2026-09-22** — prompt limits are the vendor's or there are none. Kling's
  `prompt` and `negative_prompt` rose from 2,000 to the published **2,500**;
  Wan, Wan 2.6 and Seedance lost their 2,000-character `prompt` cap and their
  1,000-character `negative_prompt` cap entirely. Nothing got stricter: every
  prompt that worked before still works, and longer ones now reach the
  provider instead of being refused here.

sections.title: Workflows
sections.heading: Workflows
sections.text:
Chain several models into one call. A **workflow** is a curated template —
"write this line, then speak it", "enhance this prompt, then generate the
image" — that we host and version. You send your inputs once, get a `run_id`
back, and poll it until the chain finishes.

Anyone can list the workflows; running one needs an API key (a guest run is
refused with `403`). Like a task, a run is polled without an auth header.

**Each step is billed as an ordinary request at that model's normal rate for
your account.** There is no workflow surcharge and no markup for chaining, and
your usage reports include the steps as ordinary traffic.

sections.title: Workflows
sections.heading: The catalog
sections.text:
| Workflow | Chain |
|---|---|
| `script-voiceover` | LLM writes a line → TTS speaks it |
| `enhance-image` | LLM writes an image prompt → image model renders it |
| `enhance-video` | LLM writes a shot description → video model renders it |
| `animate-image` | Image model generates a frame → video model animates it |
| `animate-upscale` | Image model generates → video model animates → upscaler sharpens the clip |
| `enhance-animate` | LLM writes an image prompt → image model renders it → video model animates it |
| `gen-edit` | Image model generates → image model edits that image |

`GET /v2/workflows` is the live list — public, no key needed — treat it, not
this table, as the source of truth. Each entry carries the `input_schema` your `inputs` must satisfy
(real JSON Schema), the `steps` naming every model the run will charge you
for, and the `version` your run gets pinned to — a run that starts on v2
finishes on v2. Chains that open with an LLM take a `messages` array (you
supply the idea, the workflow supplies the system instruction); the rest take
plain strings.

sections.title: Workflows
sections.heading: Run one
sections.text:
```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/workflows/script-voiceover/run \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"inputs": {
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "One upbeat line about the sea."}],
        "voice": "Serena"
      }}'
# → 202 {"run_id": "wf:...", "status": "queued", "poll_url": "/v2/workflows/runs/wf:..."}

curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/workflows/runs/wf:...
# no auth header — the run_id is an unguessable capability token, like a task_id
```

Worth knowing before you spend anything:

- **Everything is validated before the `202`**: your `inputs` against the
  workflow's schema (`422`), **every** step's model against your key's scope
  (`403`), the credit floor for the whole chain (`402`), your tier (`403`),
  and runs already in flight (`429`). A run whose *second* step would be
  denied is rejected before the first step costs you anything.
- **Poll the run**: `queued → running → completed | failed | cancelled`. Each
  step carries a real `task_id` you can also poll at `GET /v2/tasks/{task_id}`
  — a workflow step is an ordinary async task we submitted for you.
- **`output` is the last step's result.** Every intermediate output stays
  visible under `steps[]` — the enhanced prompt, the still image, whatever a
  middle step produced.
- **If a step fails, the run stops.** `failed_step_index` says where. Steps
  that already succeeded stay billed and their outputs stay visible.
- **Cancel is between steps only** (`POST .../runs/{run_id}/cancel`, key
  required): it does **not** stop the step already running — that step
  completes and bills in full; steps that had not dispatched never do. Same
  rule as ordinary inference: once a task is with a provider it cannot be
  called back.
- **Limits**: a run counts once against your rate limit, at submission — its
  steps do not. Runs in flight per account are capped (`429` past the cap).
  Media URLs in outputs are Relay-hosted and live **1 hour** unless you store
  them (below); the run record itself stays readable after they expire, so
  download what you need within the hour.
- **Storage is run-level.** Add `store_output: relay1d`, `relay7d` or
  `relay30d` to the run body and every step that produces a file stores its
  output for that long, each charged the flat per-file fee — the same option,
  the same rates and the same refusals as a single request
  ([Video → How long the link lives](video.md#how-long-the-link-lives)). Steps
  that produce text are untouched, and a run is refused up front with `422` if
  any of its media steps runs a model that does not offer storage, rather than
  storing some steps and skipping others. There is no per-step override.
  A stored step stays pollable at `GET /v2/tasks/{task_id}` for as long as its
  output.
- **Or be called when it ends.** Add `webhook_url` to the run body and we POST
  the finished run to it once: `workflow.completed`, or `workflow.failed` for
  a run that failed or was cancelled (`result.status` says which). The payload
  carries the run exactly as the poll returns it, signed and retried like task
  webhooks; the same URL rules apply (`https`, a public host, `422`
  otherwise). The steps themselves send no webhooks. Details:
  [Tasks & Webhooks → Workflow run webhooks](../reference/async-webhooks.md#workflow-run-webhooks).

sections.title: Workflows
sections.heading: Today's boundaries
sections.text:
Templates are curated by us (you cannot define your own chain); chains are
linear (no branches, conditionals, or parallel steps); no per-step retries or
fallback models beyond the provider failover every request already gets; no
streaming; no mid-step cancellation; no per-step storage override; no
per-step webhooks (the run sends one when it ends).

Need one of these, or a chain that isn't in the catalog?
[Tell us](mailto:info@opengpu.network) — what people ask for drives what we
add next.

sections.title: Auth & Access
sections.heading: Auth & Access
sections.text:
Relay takes three kinds of credential: an **API key** for inference, a
**dashboard login (JWT)** for account and key management, and **none** for
guest access. Which routes take which:

| Credential | Header | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| API key (`relay_sk_...`) | `X-API-Key: relay_sk_...` or `Authorization: Bearer relay_sk_...` | Inference endpoints, Instances |
| Dashboard JWT | `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` | Account and key management (`/v2/customer/*`); also inference, billed to your own wallet |
| Superkey (partner tiers) | `X-API-Key: relay_sk_...` | Account and key management for your end users; see [Enterprise & Partners](../reference/enterprise.md) |
| None (guest) | — | Inference on guest-enabled models, at a strict rate limit |

sections.title: Auth & Access
sections.heading: API keys
sections.text:
Both headers work on every inference endpoint:

```bash
# Method 1: X-API-Key header
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "openai/gpt-5.4", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}'

# Method 2: Bearer token (what the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs send)
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer relay_sk_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "openai/gpt-5.4", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}'
```

If you send both headers, `X-API-Key` wins. A key that is missing, invalid or
revoked returns `401`; sending no credential at all makes you a guest.

The full key secret is shown **once, at creation**; every later listing
shows it masked. Management calls address a key by its non-secret `key_id`.
See [API Keys & Account](../reference/keys.md).

sections.title: Auth & Access
sections.heading: Dashboard / JWT auth
sections.text:
Account and management routes (`/v2/customer/*`) take a **JWT**: the session
token the dashboard holds once you sign in at
[dashboard.relaygpu.com](https://dashboard.relaygpu.com). Sign-in itself is a
dashboard flow, not part of the public API. Send the token as
`Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on management calls; it is valid for 7 days,
and signing in again issues a new one. A regular API key cannot call these
routes (`403`); on partner tiers the [superkey](../reference/enterprise.md#superkey)
can, which is the way to script key management.

A JWT can also call **inference** endpoints directly (`Authorization: Bearer
<jwt>`), billed to your account's wallet. This is how the dashboard
playground works. That usage is attributed to an automatic, read-only system
key named `__relayfront__` in your key list; see
[API Keys & Account](../reference/keys.md#the-__relayfront__-system-key).

sections.title: Auth & Access
sections.heading: Guest mode
sections.text:
No key required: omit both headers. Guests get the strictest rate limit, and
some models are key-only; a guest request for one returns `403`. Guests cannot
use `store_output` or prompt caching. `model_restrictions_per_tier.guest` in
[`GET /v2/models`](../endpoints/models.md) lists the models guests cannot call.

sections.title: Auth & Access
sections.heading: Access tiers
sections.text:
Every account is on a tier (`basic`, `pro`, `max`, or a custom partner tier;
callers without a key are `guest`). A tier sets how many keys you can hold,
your requests-per-minute limits per mode, and which models you can call.
The numbers are tuned over time, so read them live:

```bash
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/tiers
# → {"tiers": [{"tier": "basic", "max_keys": ..., "rate_limits": {"direct": ..., "opengpu": ..., "global": ...},
#               "model_restrictions": [...]}, ...],
#    "current_tier": "guest"}
```

Send your API key with that call and `current_tier` is your own tier. Rate
limits are per customer: all your API keys share one pool. See
[Rate Limits](../reference/rate-limits.md).

sections.title: Auth & Access
sections.heading: Enterprise & partner tiers
sections.text:
Building on Relay, or need more than the standard tiers? Enterprise and partner plans offer:

- Higher rate limits and key counts tuned to your workload
- Programmatic key management: provision, top up and revoke keys for your own end users, each with its own spend limit ([how it works](../reference/enterprise.md))
- Custom pricing
- [Instances](../endpoints/instances.md): rentable GPU, NPU and CPU machines on the same wallet

[Contact us](mailto:info@opengpu.network) to set one up.

sections.title: Auth & Access
sections.heading: Credits
sections.text:
Requests are billed by usage, at each model's [pricing](../endpoints/models.md).
Check your balance in the [dashboard](https://dashboard.relaygpu.com), or with
`GET /v2/customer/credits` (or the fuller `GET /v2/customer/profile`) using your
JWT. Track spend over time per key and model with
[Usage & Metrics](../reference/usage-metrics.md). You can also opt into a
low-credit warning header; see [Low-credit warnings](../reference/keys.md#low-credit-warnings).

sections.title: Quickstart
sections.heading: Quickstart
sections.text:
Make your first request in a few minutes.

**Domains:** the **API** is `https://relaygpu.com` (every curl and SDK call); the **dashboard** is `https://dashboard.relaygpu.com` (sign-up, balance, keys). Every endpoint and parameter is in the [API Explorer](../reference/api-explorer/README.md).

sections.title: Quickstart
sections.heading: 1. Get an API key
sections.text:
1. Create an account at [dashboard.relaygpu.com](https://dashboard.relaygpu.com).
2. Go to **Dashboard → Keys**.
3. Click **Create Key**.

Copy the key (`relay_sk_...`) now: it is shown only once.

No key yet? Omit the auth header and you call as a **guest**: a strict
per-minute rate limit, and some models are key-only (a guest request for one
returns `403`).

sections.title: Quickstart
sections.heading: 2. Make a request
sections.text:
**Chat:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "openai/gpt-5.4",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
  }'
```

The same call with the OpenAI Python SDK:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://relaygpu.com/v2/openai/v1", api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")
resp = client.chat.completions.create(model="openai/gpt-5.4", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}])
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```

**Image generation:** returns the image inline, base64-encoded, in `images`.
```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/image/flux/generate \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "A red fox in autumn forest"}'
```

**Video generation:** takes 2–20 minutes, so video is **asynchronous by
default**: the call returns `202` with a `task_id` to poll.
```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/video/wan-25/t2v \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "A cat walking on a beach", "duration": 5}'
# Returns: {"task_id": "direct:abc12345-...", "status": "queued", "poll_url": "/v2/tasks/direct:abc12345-...", ...}

# Poll for the result (no auth header: the task_id is the access token):
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/tasks/direct:abc12345-...
```

When `status` is `completed`, `result.videos` holds the video URLs. The result
and its links expire 1 hour after the task finishes, so fetch them promptly.
