sections.title: Tasks & Webhooks
sections.heading: Tasks & Webhooks
sections.text:
Long-running work (video, complex image jobs) runs asynchronously: submit,
get a `task_id` back immediately, then either **poll** for the result or have
us **push** it to your server via a signed webhook.

Any endpoint that supports it takes `"async": true` in the request body.
Video endpoints are async **by default** (send `"async": false` to wait
inline instead). Polling needs no auth header; webhooks need an API key.

sections.title: Tasks & Webhooks
sections.heading: Task lifecycle
sections.text:
```
queued → running → completed | failed
```

Submitting returns `202`:

```json
{"task_id": "direct:abc12345-...", "status": "queued", "poll_url": "/v2/tasks/direct:abc12345-..."}
```

**Poll** with `GET /v2/tasks/{task_id}`: no auth header needed; the task_id
itself is the (unguessable) access token. Use it (including the `direct:`
prefix and colon) literally in the path, with no URL-encoding:

```json
{
  "task_id": "direct:abc12345-...",
  "status": "completed",
  "elapsed_seconds": 10,
  "task_address": null,
  "mode": "direct",
  "model": "black-forest-labs/FLUX-2-pro",
  "created_at": "2026-07-05T14:49:06+00:00",
  "error": null,
  "result": {
    "images": ["<base64-encoded PNG>"],
    "model": "black-forest-labs/FLUX-2-pro",
    "width": 512,
    "height": 512,
    "success": true
  }
}
```

The `result` shape is model-family-specific. Image models return the media
inline as **base64** in `result.images`; video models return Relay-hosted URLs
in `result.videos` (e.g. `{"videos": ["https://cdn.relaygpu.com/content/0jTz5Ht994t1szRMSgF1JQ"], "model": "Wan-AI/Wan2.5-T2V", "size": "832x480", "duration": 5}`).
The webhook payload and the poll response carry the same links.

`elapsed_seconds` ticks while running and **freezes at the terminal state**.
A failed task carries `error` (a string) with `result` set to `null`, plus a
machine-readable `error_code` and `error_detail`; see
[Errors → Async tasks](errors.md#async-tasks).

**Long-poll instead of looping**: add `?wait=N` (a whole number of seconds,
1 to 30) and the request is held until the task is `completed` or `failed`, or
until N seconds pass, whichever comes first. The reply is the same body as an
ordinary poll, in whatever state the task is in by then, with `elapsed_seconds`
as of the reply. A task that is already finished, and an unknown or expired
`task_id` (`404`), answer at once. Any other value of `wait` returns `422`
(`VALIDATION_ERROR`). Under heavy load a waiting poll may answer at once
instead, exactly as if `wait` were absent, so keep looping until the status is
terminal. Long-polling up to 30 seconds is safe behind Cloudflare: its own
limit is far above this.

```bash
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/tasks/direct:abc12345-...?wait=30"
```

**By default your output link and the task record both live 1 hour after the
task reaches its terminal state.** After that, `GET /v2/tasks/{task_id}` returns
404 and so does the media link, though the work was still billed.

Add `store_output: relay1d`, `relay7d` or `relay30d` to a media request and
**both** live for the full 1, 7 or 30 days — the task stays pollable and the
output stays served from Relay's CDN — for a flat per-file fee. The record TTL
and the link TTL are the same number set on the same write, so they cannot drift
apart. Rates and the options offered to you are in `media_storage` at
`GET /v2/pricing`; an option missing from that block returns `422`, and the
guest tier cannot use `store_output` at all. Storage also depends on the model:
one that returns its media inline has no link to host, so check
`store_output_supported` in `GET /v2/models` — a `relay*` request against a
model that says `false` returns `422` naming it.

sections.title: Tasks & Webhooks
sections.heading: Safe retries (`Idempotency-Key`)
sections.text:
A submit that loses its connection leaves you not knowing whether the task was
accepted. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (any string, 1–255 characters — a
UUID per logical request is the usual choice) and a retry is safe:

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/video/kling-3/t2v \
  -H "X-API-Key: relay_sk_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 6f1c2a9e-5b7d-4c3e-9a8f-2d1e0b4c7a91" \
  -d '{"prompt":"a lighthouse at dusk"}'
```

- The **first** request with a key is processed as usual and returns its `202`.
- A **retry** with the same key and the same body, within **24 hours** of the
  first use, returns the original `202` again — same `task_id`, same
  `poll_url` — with the response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. No new
  task is created and nothing is charged again.
- The same key with a **different body** returns `422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.
  Use a new key for a new request.
- A retry that arrives while the first request is still being accepted returns
  `409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` with `Retry-After: 1`; retry after a second.
- Keys are scoped to your account: another account using the same key does not
  collide with yours. Guest (keyless) requests ignore the header.
- The key outlives the task record: a replay late in the 24 hours still
  returns the original `task_id`, but its poll may already be `404` once the
  result has expired (see retention above).

The key is honoured on every request that answers `202` (async submits, and
`POST /v2/workflows/{workflow_id}/run`, where a replay returns the same
`run_id`). Synchronous and streaming calls accept the header but do not replay:
they run as usual. `POST /v2/files` keeps its own `Idempotency-Key` behaviour
(a replay returns the same `file_id`).

sections.title: Tasks & Webhooks
sections.heading: Webhooks
sections.text:
Add `"webhook_url": "https://your-server.example/hook"` to an async request
and we POST the terminal payload to it. The body is the task-status payload
plus an `event` field (`task.completed` or `task.failed`).

A `webhook_url` needs an API key (guests get `422`), `"async": true`
(video has it by default) and direct mode; anything else is refused with `422`
at submit time.

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/video/wan-25/t2v \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "A robot waving", "async": true,
       "webhook_url": "https://your-server.example/hook"}'
```

The webhook body carries **field-set parity** with the poll response, not byte
parity: it omits the unused key. A completed task carries `result` and no
`error`; a failed task carries `error` and no `result`. The poll `GET` instead
returns **both** keys with one set to `null`. `task_address` is always `null`
for webhooks; they fire only for direct-mode tasks.

`error` is a human-readable string, not an object; don't code against
`error.message` or `error.code`. Branch on the sibling `error_code` instead.

The body does **not** carry `poll_url`. If you need the full result (for
example after `"result_omitted": true`), poll `GET /v2/tasks/{task_id}` using
the `task_id` from the body.

No second request is needed for total payloads up to 1 MiB (the full envelope,
result included); larger results arrive with `"result_omitted": true` and the
`result` key omitted. Fetch those from the poll URL right away (see expiry
above).

**`task.completed`**: has `result`, no `error` key:

```json
{
  "event": "task.completed",
  "task_id": "direct:3023013b-...",
  "status": "completed",
  "elapsed_seconds": 6,
  "task_address": null,
  "mode": "direct",
  "model": "Qwen/qwen-image",
  "created_at": "2026-07-06T10:23:02.962460+00:00",
  "result": { "urls": ["https://..."], "model": "Qwen/qwen-image", "size": "1024x1024", "success": true }
}
```

**`task.failed`**: `error` is a plain string, with `error_code` and `error_detail` beside it, and no `result` key:

```json
{
  "event": "task.failed",
  "task_id": "direct:...",
  "status": "failed",
  "elapsed_seconds": 1205,
  "task_address": null,
  "mode": "direct",
  "model": "Wan-AI/Wan2.5-T2V",
  "created_at": "2026-07-06T10:20:00+00:00",
  "error": "Video generation timed out.",
  "error_code": "UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT",
  "error_detail": null
}
```

**`result_omitted` thin envelope**: result > 1 MiB, so no `result` and no `error` key:

```json
{
  "event": "task.completed",
  "task_id": "direct:...",
  "status": "completed",
  "elapsed_seconds": 42,
  "task_address": null,
  "mode": "direct",
  "model": "Wan-AI/Wan2.5-T2V",
  "created_at": "2026-07-06T10:20:00+00:00",
  "result_omitted": true
}
```

sections.title: Tasks & Webhooks
sections.heading: Workflow run webhooks
sections.text:
A [workflow](../endpoints/workflows.md) run takes the same `webhook_url`, on
the run body, and is called **once**, when the run ends:

| Event | When | `result.status` |
|---|---|---|
| `workflow.completed` | the last step finished | `completed` |
| `workflow.failed` | a step failed, the run ran out of time, or you cancelled it | `failed` or `cancelled` |

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/workflows/script-voiceover/run \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"inputs": {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "One upbeat line about the sea."}],
                  "voice": "Serena"},
       "webhook_url": "https://your-server.example/hook"}'
```

The envelope is the task one: `task_id` is the **run id**, `status` is always
`completed` (the delivery finished, not necessarily the run), `mode` is
`workflows`, `model` is the workflow id, and `result` is the run **exactly as
`GET /v2/workflows/runs/{run_id}` returns it**. Branch on `event` or on
`result.status`, never on the top-level `status`:

```json
{
  "event": "workflow.failed",
  "task_id": "wf:7c9e6679-7425-40de-944b-e07fc1f90ae7",
  "status": "completed",
  "elapsed_seconds": 14,
  "task_address": null,
  "mode": "workflows",
  "model": "script-voiceover",
  "created_at": "2026-10-06T23:59:17+00:00",
  "result": {
    "run_id": "wf:7c9e6679-7425-40de-944b-e07fc1f90ae7",
    "workflow_id": "script-voiceover",
    "version": 1,
    "status": "cancelled",
    "steps": [
      {"step_index": 0, "step_id": "write", "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001",
       "status": "completed", "task_id": "direct:...", "output": {"...": "..."},
       "error": null, "cost_usd": 0.0004},
      {"step_index": 1, "step_id": "speak", "model": "Qwen/qwen3-tts-flash",
       "status": "skipped", "task_id": "direct:...", "output": null,
       "error": null, "cost_usd": null}
    ],
    "inputs": {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "One upbeat line about the sea."}], "voice": "Serena"},
    "store_output": "provider",
    "output": null,
    "error": "Cancelled by request.",
    "failed_step_index": null,
    "total_cost_usd": 0.0004,
    "created_at": "2026-10-06T23:59:17+00:00",
    "completed_at": "2026-10-06T23:59:31+00:00"
  }
}
```

- Signed, retried and logged exactly like task webhooks (below), with the
  same `webhook_url` rules; `422` at submit time if the URL is refused.
- One delivery per run. The run's steps never send `task.*` events of their
  own; each step's `task_id` stays pollable as usual.
- `cost_usd` per step comes from billing, which settles a second or two after
  a step finishes, so the last step can read `null` in the webhook. Poll the
  run for the settled figures.
- Past the 1 MiB inline cap the body carries `"result_omitted": true` instead
  of `result`; read the run from `GET /v2/workflows/runs/{run_id}`.

sections.title: Tasks & Webhooks
sections.heading: Verifying deliveries
sections.text:
Every delivery is signed per the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/)
spec: headers `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature`. Your
signing secret is auto-provisioned; fetch it anytime. Auth: JWT, or
(enterprise/partner) superkey; regular inference keys can't read it:

```bash
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/webhook-secret \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT"
# → {"secret": "whsec_...", "created_at": "...", "previous_valid_until": null}
```

The signing secret is **account-level**: every API key on your account,
including partner sub-keys, shares it; there is no per-key secret.

Off-the-shelf `standardwebhooks` libraries verify with the full `whsec_...`
string:

```python
from standardwebhooks import Webhook

wh = Webhook("whsec_...")
payload = wh.verify(request_body_bytes, request_headers)  # raises if invalid
```

Rolling your own? The HMAC-SHA256 key is the **base64-decoded part after
`whsec_`**; sign the exact string `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}`
and compare (constant-time) against each space-delimited `v1,<base64>` token.
`webhook-timestamp` is an integer Unix epoch in **seconds** (UTC); reject
timestamps outside your tolerance (we recommend 5 minutes).

Rotate with `POST /v2/customer/webhook-secret/rotate`; the old secret keeps
verifying for 24h (deliveries carry both signatures during the grace window).
Only the two most recent secrets are ever valid: rotating again within the
grace window immediately drops the oldest one, so rotating twice in quick
succession retires the first secret before its 24h elapses. Roll one secret at
a time and let the grace window pass before rotating again.

sections.title: Tasks & Webhooks
sections.heading: Delivery guarantees
sections.text:
- **At-least-once.** `webhook-id` is stable across retries; dedupe on it.
- A `2xx` within 15 seconds acks. Anything else (3xx included; redirects are
  not followed) retries: up to 8 attempts, backoff 30s doubling to a 30-minute
  cap (~1h window). After that the event is dropped. Fall back to the poll
  URL, but it also expires ~1h after completion (see **Reconciliation** below),
  so don't treat it as permanent.
- `webhook_url` must be `https://`, publicly resolvable, and without embedded
  credentials, checked at submit time (422 if not).

sections.title: Tasks & Webhooks
sections.heading: Delivery log
sections.text:
Every attempt we make is recorded and queryable; when a webhook "didn't
arrive", look here before your receiver's logs:

```bash
# Recent deliveries, newest first
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/webhook-deliveries?limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT"

# Everything that exhausted its retries
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/webhook-deliveries?outcome=gave_up" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT"

# Full attempt-by-attempt timeline for one task (or one workflow run: wf:...)
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/webhook-deliveries/direct:abc12345-..." \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT"
```

- **Filters**: `outcome` (`delivered` / `failed` / `gave_up` / `blocked`),
  `event` (`task.completed` / `task.failed` / `workflow.completed` /
  `workflow.failed`), `task_id` (**exact** match; paste the full id, prefixes
  return nothing). A workflow run's delivery is listed under its run id
  (`wf:...`) in `task_id`, and the timeline route takes a run id the same way.
- **Pagination**: cursor-based, with `limit` (default 20, max 100); pass the
  response's `next_page` back as `page` while `has_more` is true.
- The per-task timeline lists each attempt with its outcome and, where
  recorded, the receiver's HTTP status or the transport error. `404` means no
  deliveries were recorded for that `task_id` (e.g. the request had no
  `webhook_url`).
- Auth: JWT, or (enterprise/partner) superkey.

sections.title: Tasks & Webhooks
sections.heading: Writing your handler
sections.text:
Verify the signature, dedupe on `webhook-id` (delivery is at-least-once),
enqueue the event, and return any `2xx` within the 15-second ack budget. Never
do heavy processing inline: fetching a large result or any slow work inside
the handler can blow the 15s budget and trigger duplicate retries.

sections.title: Tasks & Webhooks
sections.heading: Reconciliation
sections.text:
The retry window (~61.5 min: the first attempt at completion, then retries
30s, 60s, 120s, 240s, 480s, 960s and 1800s apart) and the 60-minute result TTL
both run from task completion, so the poll
URL actually 404s ~90s **before** the final webhook attempt. If your receiver
is unreachable for the whole window you lose **both** the webhook and the
pollable result while the work is still billed.

Protect yourself: persist submitted `task_id`s, sweep for any task with no
terminal webhook after a few minutes, and poll before the 1-hour expiry. A
10-minute outage is fine; a 2-hour outage means data loss unless the sweeper
caught it first. After the fact, the [delivery log](#delivery-log)
(`?outcome=gave_up`) tells you exactly which tasks you lost.

Full contract (payload schema, headers): [API Explorer → Webhooks](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer).

sections.title: Enterprise & Partners
sections.heading: Enterprise & Partners
sections.text:
Enterprise and partner plans add higher rate limits and key counts, custom
pricing, and the tools to build on Relay: issue API keys to your own users, cap
each key's spend, restrict the models they can call, and pull per-key usage to
bill them. [Talk to us](mailto:info@opengpu.network) to set one up.

The standard keys, usage, and metrics endpoints behave the same on these
plans; see [API Keys & Account](keys.md) and [Usage & Metrics](usage-metrics.md).
This page covers what they add on top.

sections.title: Enterprise & Partners
sections.heading: Superkey
sections.text:
On a partner tier, your account's first key is your **superkey**, the
management credential for your backend. Use it to mint, top up, and revoke keys and to read your account
(`X-API-Key` on the `/v2/customer/*` routes); it's flagged `is_superkey` in your
key list. Every other key you issue is inference-only, so a leaked one can't
touch your account or the other keys.

**Rotating the superkey** (routine hygiene, or it leaked): revoke it, then
crown a replacement with `POST /v2/customer/keys/{key_id}/promote` on any
active key. Promote is **JWT-only** by design (a stolen superkey can't crown
its own successor) and returns `409` while an active superkey still exists,
so revoke first. Between the two calls your backend cannot manage keys with a
superkey (your dashboard login still can, and your issued keys keep serving
inference); have the replacement key ready before you revoke.

sections.title: Enterprise & Partners
sections.heading: Per-key budgets
sections.text:
Give any key a spending cap with `key_budget`. When it runs out, that key's
requests return `402 KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` until you top it up, so a single user
can never drain your balance. Omit it to leave a key uncapped.

```bash
# Superkey issues a key with a $5 cap
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/keys \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_SUPERKEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "end_user_42", "key_budget": 5.00}'

# Top it up later
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/keys/{key_id}/topup \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_SUPERKEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"amount": 2.00}'
```

To change a cap, `PATCH /v2/customer/keys/{key_id}` with `key_budget`, which is
tri-state: a number **sets** the cap absolutely, an explicit `null` **removes**
it (uncapped), and omitting the field leaves it unchanged. Use `/topup` for
increments (it's concurrency-safe; PATCH just overwrites).

sections.title: Enterprise & Partners
sections.heading: Model access
sections.text:
Restrict every issued key to an approved list of models; your superkey keeps
full access.

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/model-allowlist \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_SUPERKEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model_allowlist": ["direct.openai.openai/gpt-5.2"]}'
```

Send `{"model_allowlist": null}` to remove the restriction.

Read the current allowlist with `GET /v2/customer/model-allowlist` (returns
`{ "model_allowlist": [...] | null }`):

```bash
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/model-allowlist \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_SUPERKEY"
```

It's also included as `sub_key_model_allowlist` on `GET /v2/customer/profile`
if you're loading the whole account at once.

sections.title: Enterprise & Partners
sections.heading: Per-key cost
sections.text:
`GET /v2/customer/usage/timeseries` breaks down cost and tokens by model and by
key over any date range: the report you need to bill your users. It takes the
same query parameters as [metrics](usage-metrics.md#metrics) but returns
spend instead of latency; group by key for a per-user total.

This endpoint is **partner-tier only**: it requires a custom (partner) tier.
Calls from standard tiers return `403` — use `GET /v2/customer/usage` (per-key
lifetime/daily totals) instead. The latency [metrics](usage-metrics.md#metrics)
endpoint, by contrast, is available on **every** tier.

```bash
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/usage/timeseries?start_time=1783000800&bucket_width=1d&group_by=model&group_by=key_id" \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_SUPERKEY"
```

sections.title: Enterprise & Partners
sections.heading: Low-credit warnings
sections.text:
The account [low-credit warning](keys.md#low-credit-warnings) covers
every key. With it on, the keys you issue also receive the `X-Credit-Warning`
header, so your users can see the account is low. To keep your balance private,
leave it off and check `GET /v2/customer/credits` from your backend instead.

sections.title: Enterprise & Partners
sections.heading: Pricing
sections.text:
Enterprise and partner accounts can have custom per-model rates.
`GET /v2/customer/pricing` (JWT or superkey) returns your effective pricing;
the public `GET /v2/pricing` never shows it. Standard tiers get `403` there and
pay the public rates.

---

Full endpoint reference:
[API Explorer](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer).

sections.title: Errors
sections.heading: Errors
sections.text:
Every error response carries **two** things: the `detail` field Relay has always
returned, and an additive `error` object with a machine-readable code.

```json
{
  "detail": "KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: this API key's budget is depleted. Topup via POST /v2/customer/keys/{key}/topup.",
  "error": {
    "code": "KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED",
    "type": "authorization",
    "source": "client",
    "message": "KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: this API key's budget is depleted. Topup via POST /v2/customer/keys/{key}/topup.",
    "request_id": "3f0c9c8e-6a1d-4b77-9a2e-2b4f1e77c001"
  }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `code` | Stable token to branch on. **May be `null`** — see below. |
| `type` | Broad class: `validation`, `authentication`, `authorization`, `rate_limit`, `timeout`, `schema`, `internal`, `unavailable`, `removed`. `null` when `code` is. |
| `source` | Best-effort blame: `client`, `provider`, `relay`. Advisory — see the caveat below. `null` when `code` is. |
| `message` | The same text as `detail` (or, when `detail` is structured, a one-line summary of it). |
| `request_id` | Matches the `X-Request-ID` response header. Quote it in support requests. |

`detail` is **unchanged** and will stay that way. If you parse it today, keep
parsing it — nothing about its wording, type, or position has moved. The `error`
object is purely additive. Request-validation errors (`422`
`VALIDATION_ERROR`) still return a list in FastAPI's standard shape, and the
full list is preserved under `error.detail`. Each entry names the field
(`loc`) and the problem (`msg`); it never echoes the value you sent, in any
environment:

```json
{"detail": [{"type": "missing", "loc": ["body", "prompt"], "msg": "Field required"}]}
```

sections.title: Errors
sections.heading: What to rely on
sections.text:
**`error.code` is append-only.** Once a code appears in the table below it will
never be renamed or removed, so matching on one is safe indefinitely. New codes
*will* be added as more of the API is classified — treat a code you do not
recognise as its HTTP status and move on.

**`error.code` can be `null`, and null does not mean "no error".** It means that
particular failure has not been classified yet. The HTTP status is always
authoritative; the code is the finer-grained discriminator where we have one.
Branch on the status first, then refine on the code.

**`source` is a best-effort classification, not an audit.** It is inherited from
how the upstream provider reported the failure. Providers that answer a
bad-parameter error with an HTTP 5xx are reported as `source: "provider"` even
though the request was at fault — we deliberately do not second-guess the
upstream signal. Do not gate billing, alerting, or retry decisions on `source`
alone; use `code` and the status.

sections.title: Errors
sections.heading: `error.detail` on content and image errors
sections.text:
`error.detail` always carries upstream's own verdict, **verbatim and
uninterpreted**, beside our reading of it — so you can check the two against
each other. Its shape depends on how upstream said it, and there are two:

sections.title: Errors
sections.heading: Image lane — the model's own verdict fields
sections.text:
`CONTENT_POLICY_DECLINED`, `IMAGE_TEXT_RESPONSE` and `IMAGE_NO_OUTPUT` on the
image endpoints carry:

| field | what it is |
|---|---|
| `finish_reason` | the model's own verdict (`STOP`, `SAFETY`, `OTHER`, …), exactly as it appears on a successful Gemini response |
| `block_reason` | upstream's reason for blocking the *input*, when it named one |
| `text` | the model's reply in words, when it wrote one instead of an image (capped at 400 characters) |

All three keys are always present and carry `null` where upstream reported
nothing — which is most of them, since only the Gemini models forward any of it.
Our `code` is our reading of these values; the fields are the values themselves,
so you can always check the two against each other.

**`finish_reason: STOP` does not mean the image was produced.** A model that
withholds an image on content grounds may report `STOP` and put its explanation
in `text` rather than naming a safety verdict — so a `STOP` can legitimately
arrive under a 4xx. Where that happens the `code`, not the reason, is the thing
to trust.

Do not branch on any of the three. `code` is the stable contract; these are
upstream vocabulary that can change without notice, and our mapping from them is
an interpretation that may be revised.

sections.title: Errors
sections.heading: Video and chat lanes — the provider's filter code
sections.text:
Where a provider's content filter refuses the request outright rather than the
model declining it, `CONTENT_POLICY_DECLINED` carries the filter's own verdict
instead:

| field | what it is |
|---|---|
| `upstream_code` | the provider's machine code for the refusal, verbatim (e.g. `InputImageSensitiveContentDetected.PrivacyInformation`, `DataInspectionFailed`), or `null` where the provider declined in words and named no code |
| `filtered` | `"input"`, `"output"`, or `null` when the provider did not say which |

`filtered` is the one field worth acting on, and it decides whether a retry is
worth anything:

- **`"input"`** — your prompt, reference image or reference video tripped the
  filter. Change the input.
- **`"output"`** — the input was accepted and the *generated* result was
  withheld. Rephrasing and retrying can succeed.
- **`null`** — the provider named a refusal but not a side. Treat it as either.

Read `message` alongside it, because the two carry different certainties. Where
the provider stated its verdict, an `"input"` decline is deterministic and the
message says so ("Retrying unchanged will fail"). Where the provider refused
without naming a reason — some video models only report that nothing was
produced for the prompt — the message hedges ("most likely") and a retry may
be worth one attempt. We never assert a verdict the provider did not give.

Both shapes are the same `code` and the same 422. Tell them apart by which
KEYS are present — `upstream_code`/`filtered` versus
`finish_reason`/`block_reason`/`text` — not by which values are non-null: every
key in both shapes can carry `null`, because a provider that explains nothing
is reported as explaining nothing rather than guessed at. Do not branch on the
provider's literal values.

sections.title: Errors
sections.heading: Using it from an SDK
sections.text:
The `error` object's field names (`code`, `type`, `message`) match the shape the
official OpenAI SDK already parses, so on `/v2/openai/*` endpoints you get the
code without any extra work. With `openai>=2.35`:

```python
import openai

client = openai.OpenAI(api_key="relay_sk_...",
                       base_url="https://relaygpu.com/v2/openai/v1")
try:
    client.chat.completions.create(model="openai/gpt-5.4",
                                   messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}])
except openai.APIStatusError as e:
    print(e.status_code)   # 402
    print(e.code)          # "KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED"
    print(e.body["source"])  # "client"
```

The `anthropic` SDK exposes the same values one level in, as
`e.body["error"]["code"]`.

**Exception classes are unchanged.** Both SDKs pick the exception class from the
HTTP status, and no status changed — an `AuthenticationError` is still an
`AuthenticationError`. What *does* change: because `error.message` now exists,
both SDKs prefer it when rendering the exception, so the text in your logs and
tracebacks is more specific than before. Nothing to migrate; expect nicer
strings.

sections.title: Errors
sections.heading: Rollout note
sections.text:
The `error` object appears on **every** error response at once — including
routes whose `code` is still `null`. Migration is incremental for the code
*values*, never for the envelope. If you validate response bodies against a
strict schema that rejects unknown keys, add `error` to it before upgrading.

sections.title: Errors
sections.heading: Status codes
sections.text:
| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|------|---------|------------|
| `400` | The upstream model rejected the request parameters (`UPSTREAM_INVALID_REQUEST`), or a well-formed request asks for something the route cannot do — `stream` with `async`, a direct-only route in `opengpu` mode, an unknown cursor (`VALIDATION_ERROR` at 400) | Fix the request; `detail` says what |
| `401` | API key missing, invalid, or revoked | The message says which; use an active key or contact your key issuer |
| `402` | Out of credits (wallet, or this key's budget) | Top up |
| `403` | Valid key, access denied | The message names the blocking layer (tier, allowlist, or account state) |
| `404` | Unknown route, or an unknown key / task / run / file | Check the endpoint tables per category. `FILE_NOT_FOUND`: the file id is not yours, or it expired more than 24 hours ago |
| `409` | Conflicts with current state (e.g. a superkey already exists) | Resolve the conflict, then retry |
| `410` | Gone for good (e.g. an expired or fully-redeemed promo code) | Do not retry |
| `413` | The uploaded file is too large (`FILE_TOO_LARGE`) | [Files](../endpoints/files.md) take up to 100 MB per file — send a smaller file |
| `415` | The uploaded file is not an image, video or audio file (`FILE_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED`) | Upload media only; for a URL upload, check what the URL actually serves |
| `422` | The body failed schema validation (`VALIDATION_ERROR` at 422), the model declined it on content grounds, or it replied in words instead of an image | `VALIDATION_ERROR`: `detail` lists the offending fields (the same code answers 400 when the body is well-formed but the route cannot serve it — branch on the code, not the status). `CONTENT_POLICY_DECLINED`: the content was refused — change the content, not the parameters. Check `detail.filtered`: `"input"` means a retry of the same input will fail again, `"output"` means rephrasing can succeed. Where no side is named, borderline content is not always declined deterministically, so a retry may succeed. `IMAGE_TEXT_RESPONSE`: read `detail.text` — the model's own reply says whether it declined or answered a question. `VALIDATION_ERROR` with a `store_output` message: the option is not offered right now, or that MODEL returns media inline and has nothing to store (the message names it; `store_output_supported` in `GET /v2/models` says which models offer it) — send the request without it, or with the default `provider` |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded, or the daily free upload quota is used up | Back off; `Retry-After` header is set. `FILE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`: free (`relay1h`) [Files](../endpoints/files.md) uploads are used up for today — `Retry-After` counts to 00:00 UTC; a paid retention is not limited by the quota |
| `500` | Relay-side error | Retry; contact support with the `request_id` if it persists |
| `502` | A provider failed the request, none could take it, or one answered with nothing usable | `UPSTREAM_ERROR`: a provider accepted this request and failed while serving it. Retry; if it persists, contact support with the `request_id`. `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`: no provider could take this request right now — none is registered for the model, every one is paused after repeated failures, your tier cannot wait for a busy one, or the provider we reached refused the call outright (quota, balance, rate limit). Retry later. `IMAGE_NO_OUTPUT`: the call succeeded and the model produced no image — retry once, then change the prompt or reference image |
| `503` | Model temporarily at capacity, or Instances is unavailable | `CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED`: every provider for the model is busy — retry after `Retry-After` seconds. `INSTANCES_UNAVAILABLE`: instance rental is not configured on this environment, or the instance catalog is temporarily unreadable — retry after `Retry-After` seconds; if it persists, contact support |
| `504` | Upstream timeout | Retry; use `"async": true` for long tasks |

sections.title: Errors
sections.heading: Examples
sections.text:
The `error` object is abbreviated below — it is present in full on all of them.

**422 (model declined the content)** — `CONTENT_POLICY_DECLINED`:
```json
{
  "detail": "The model declined this request — its content policy was triggered by the prompt or a reference image. Adjust and retry.",
  "error": {
    "code": "CONTENT_POLICY_DECLINED",
    "detail": {"finish_reason": "SAFETY"}
  }
}
```
This is the model's own refusal, not a Relay policy check and not a validation
failure. It is returned on the image endpoints when the provider answers
successfully but produces no image. Note that a reference image can trigger it
on its own, with a prompt that is fine.

The message is hedged when the model gave no explicit safety verdict but did
generate an image that was then withheld:

```json
{
  "detail": "The generated image was withheld, most likely by the provider's content policy — adjust the prompt or reference image and retry.",
  "error": {
    "code": "CONTENT_POLICY_DECLINED",
    "detail": {"finish_reason": "OTHER"}
  }
}
```

Borderline content is **not** always deterministic — the same request can be
declined once and succeed on a retry. Treat a single decline as a signal about
the content, not a verdict on it.

**422 (model replied in words)** — `IMAGE_TEXT_RESPONSE`:
```json
{
  "detail": "The model replied with text instead of an image; its reply is in error.detail.text. That usually means it declined the content, or the prompt read as a question rather than an instruction to generate an image.",
  "error": {
    "code": "IMAGE_TEXT_RESPONSE",
    "detail": {
      "finish_reason": "STOP",
      "block_reason": null,
      "text": "I cannot create images of official identification documents, including passports."
    }
  }
}
```
The provider answered normally; the model just wrote a sentence where the image
belonged. Two very different things arrive in this identical shape — a content
refusal, and a prompt the model read as a question and simply answered — so the
code deliberately does not choose between them and hands you the reply instead.
`detail.text` is the diagnosis: if it reads as a refusal, change the content; if
it reads as an answer, phrase the prompt as an instruction to generate an image.

**502 (model produced no image)** — `IMAGE_NO_OUTPUT`:
```json
{
  "detail": "The model returned no image for this request. If it repeats with the same input, adjust the prompt or the reference image.",
  "error": {
    "code": "IMAGE_NO_OUTPUT",
    "detail": {"finish_reason": null}
  }
}
```
Distinct from `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`: the provider call succeeded, and the
response simply carried no image.

**502 (a provider failed the request)** — `UPSTREAM_ERROR`:
```json
{
  "detail": "Upstream service error. Contact support with request_id=direct:… if this persists.",
  "error": {
    "code": "UPSTREAM_ERROR",
    "detail": {"upstream_code": "model_server_error"}
  }
}
```
A provider accepted this request and failed while serving it. Retry; if it
persists, contact support with the `request_id`. `detail.upstream_code` is the
provider's own machine code where it sent one, `null` where it did not — it is
reported, never interpreted. `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` carries the same field when
a provider answered but refused the call (quota, balance, rate limit); it is
absent when no provider was reached at all, which is itself the distinction.

This is the half of 502 where a provider took the request and then broke.
`PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` is the other half: **no provider could take this request
right now** — none is registered for the model, every one is paused after
repeated failures, your tier cannot wait for a busy one, or the provider we
reached refused the call outright (quota, balance, rate limit). Retry later. The line between them is whether anything was *served*,
not whether anything answered. The prefixes carry it throughout: `UPSTREAM_*`
means the provider answered badly while serving (`UPSTREAM_ERROR`,
`UPSTREAM_INVALID_REQUEST`, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`); `PROVIDER_*` describes whether
any provider could serve you at all.

**401 (invalid or revoked key)** — `INVALID_API_KEY` / `KEY_REVOKED`:
```json
{"detail": "Invalid API key"}
```
```json
{"detail": "This API key has been revoked. Use an active key or contact the key issuer."}
```

**402 (two variants)** — `INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS` when the account wallet is
empty, `KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` when a partner sub-key's own budget is depleted:
```json
{"detail": "Insufficient credits for this model. Top up your account to continue."}
```
```json
{"detail": "KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: this API key's budget is depleted. Topup via POST /v2/customer/keys/{key}/topup."}
```

> **Avoid the surprise:** opt into an `X-Credit-Warning: true` response header
> *before* your wallet hits `402`; see
> [Low-credit warnings](keys.md#low-credit-warnings).

**403 (the message names what blocked you)** — `SCOPE_DENIED`,
`MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the model is not served at all, or
`TIER_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE` when a guest request asks for `store_output` storage:
```json
{"detail": "Your tier does not have access to openai.openai/gpt-5.4 in direct mode"}
```
```json
{"detail": "direct.openai.openai/gpt-5.4 is blocked by your account's model allowlist (set by your key issuer). Allowed models: direct.anthropic.anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001"}
```
```json
{"detail": "openai.openai/gpt-5.4 is not available for unauthenticated (guest) access. Provide an API key (X-API-Key header) to use this model."}
```

**400 (upstream rejected the request itself)** — `UPSTREAM_INVALID_REQUEST`,
where the message comes from the model provider's own validation:
```json
{"detail": "Invalid param: Could not finish the message because max_tokens or model output limit was reached. Please try again with higher max_tokens."}
```

**429 (rate limited)** — `RATE_LIMITED`, with `Retry-After: 60` header:
```json
{"detail": "Rate limit exceeded: 16/15 RPM for direct mode (tier: basic)"}
```

**503 (at capacity)** — `CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED`, with `Retry-After: 5` header:
```json
{"detail": "Model temporarily at capacity. Please retry later."}
```

sections.title: Errors
sections.heading: Async tasks
sections.text:
A failed task's poll response (and the matching failure webhook) carries the
same trio as the synchronous envelope: the human `error` string, a
machine-readable `error_code`, and `error_detail` — the structured payload that
appears as `error.detail` on a synchronous response.

```json
{
  "task_id": "direct:7b4b4241-e024-4a65-b490-c200b871b989",
  "status": "failed",
  "error": "Provider error 500: Failed to download https://example.com/x.png",
  "error_code": "PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE",
  "error_detail": null
}
```

On an image task that produced nothing, `error_detail` carries the model's own
verdict — the same `{"finish_reason": ..., "block_reason": ..., "text": ...}`
object described above:

```json
{
  "status": "failed",
  "error": "The generated image was withheld, most likely by the provider's content policy — adjust the prompt or reference image and retry.",
  "error_code": "CONTENT_POLICY_DECLINED",
  "error_detail": {"finish_reason": "OTHER", "block_reason": null, "text": null}
}
```

Both keys are always present and are `null` on tasks that failed before they
shipped, and on failures that carry no structured detail.

Streaming responses that fail before the first chunk keep their existing
OpenAI-shaped error body, `{"error": {"message": ..., "type": ...}}`, with no
`detail` key; where `error.code` is present it is the numeric HTTP status, not
a catalog code. That surface is deliberately unchanged so SDK stream parsing
keeps working.

In the OpenAPI spec the error envelope is the `RelayErrorResponse` schema and this stream body is `StreamErrorResponse`.

For per-endpoint response schemas, see the [API Explorer](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer).

sections.title: API Keys & Account
sections.heading: API Keys & Account
sections.text:
Your account holds your API keys, your profile and your credit balance. The
routes on this page take your dashboard **JWT** (or, on partner tiers, your
[superkey](enterprise.md#superkey)); a regular API key gets `403`.

sections.title: API Keys & Account
sections.heading: Key basics
sections.text:
Mint keys in the [dashboard](https://dashboard.relaygpu.com) or via the API:

```bash
curl -X POST https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "production"}'
# → {"key": "relay_sk_...", "key_id": "key_1a2b3c...", ...}
```

`YOUR_JWT` is your dashboard session token; see
[Dashboard / JWT auth](../introduction/authentication.md#dashboard-jwt-auth).
On partner tiers the superkey works in its place.

- The full secret (`relay_sk_...`) is returned **once, at mint**; store it
  then. Every later listing shows it masked.
- Every key has a non-secret **`key_id`**; use it to address the key in all
  management calls (`PATCH`, `/revoke`, `/topup`, `/usage/{key_id}`, ...). The
  secret is **not** accepted in a URL path (a `relay_sk_...` there returns
  `400`) — it would leak into logs and proxies; address keys by `key_id`.
- **Edit a key** with `PATCH /v2/customer/keys/{key_id}`, sending only what
  you're changing: `name` (400 on duplicate) and/or `restrictions` (per-key
  model blacklist + rate limits, each at or below your tier's limit, otherwise
  `400`; the object is **replaced**, not merged). Partner tiers can also change `key_budget`; see
  [Enterprise & Partners](enterprise.md#per-key-budgets).
- Lost a secret? Revoke the key and mint a new one.
- Revoking is **reversible** (`/unrevoke`); `DELETE` on a revoked key is the
  permanent operation.

sections.title: API Keys & Account
sections.heading: Listing keys
sections.text:
`GET /v2/customer/keys` lists your keys (newest first, secrets masked). Auth:
JWT or superkey.

```bash
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/keys?limit=100" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT"
```

- **Filter**: `status=active|revoked` and/or `name=<exact>`. The `name` filter
  doubles as the by-name lookup (returns just the matching key).
- **Search**: `name_prefix=<prefix>` matches names starting with the prefix
  (case-insensitive), built for large key fleets (one key per app or end
  user). Mutually exclusive with `name`.
- **Superkey**: `is_superkey=true` returns only the account superkey (`false`
  excludes it). Combine with `status` — `?is_superkey=true&status=active&limit=1`
  answers "does an active superkey exist?" from `total`, no paging needed.
- **Paginate**: cursor-based, stable under concurrent mint/revoke. Pass `limit`
  (default 100, max 1000); when `has_more` is `true`, pass the returned
  `next_cursor` as `starting_after` for the next page:

```bash
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/keys?limit=100&starting_after=key_1a2b3c" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT"
```

Response envelope: `{ total, max_allowed, limit, has_more, next_cursor, keys }`.

sections.title: API Keys & Account
sections.heading: The `__relayfront__` system key
sections.text:
Inference fired from the dashboard (with your login session, no API key) is
attributed to an automatic system key named `__relayfront__` — you'll see it
in `GET /keys` and `GET /usage` with `"system": true` once you've used the
dashboard playground. It is not a usable credential and it's read-only:
rename/revoke/delete/promote/topup return `400`, and it never counts toward
your tier's key limit. Key names starting with `__` are reserved for system
keys, so your own keys can't collide with it.

sections.title: API Keys & Account
sections.heading: Your profile
sections.text:
`GET /v2/customer/profile` returns your own account: profile, tier, and
credit balance. Authenticate with your **JWT**, or (on enterprise/partner
accounts) your **superkey**. Regular inference keys can't read account
routes.
`GET /v2/customer/credits` returns just the balance, same auth.

```bash
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/profile \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT"
```

`ProfileResponse` fields: `customer_id`, `name`, `email`, `email_verified`,
`tier`, `status`, `created_at`, `credits`, `tier_details`,
`sub_key_model_allowlist`, `warning_threshold`. `tier_details` carries `max_api_keys`,
`current_keys`, `rate_limits`, `model_restrictions`, and the partner-feature
flags `is_custom` / `allow_subkeys`. `sub_key_model_allowlist` is the current
customer-wide [model allowlist](enterprise.md#model-access) (`null` unless
you're on a partner tier and have set one).

This is the authoritative way to check which tier you're on; the public
`model_restrictions_per_tier` matrix tells you what each tier can call, not
which one is yours. `tier_details.is_custom` tells you whether it's a partner
(enterprise) tier.

sections.title: API Keys & Account
sections.heading: Low-credit warnings
sections.text:
Opt into a heads-up before you run dry. Set a per-account **`warning_threshold`**
(in credits); while your wallet balance is below it, **every inference
response carries the header `X-Credit-Warning: true`** (a flag, no amount),
whether it was authenticated with an API key or your dashboard login.
Account and management routes never carry it. `0` (the default) turns it off.

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/settings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"warning_threshold": 20}'
```

- It's the **soft** counterpart to the hard `402` (out of credits): a nudge to
  top up while you're still being served. The header only ever appears while
  you're below the line, so treat "header present" as "top up soon".
- Auth: JWT, or (enterprise/partner) your superkey. `warning_threshold` must be
  `≥ 0` (`422` otherwise).
- **Enterprise & partner accounts:** the flag is account-wide, so the keys you
  issue carry it too. Details in [Enterprise & Partners](enterprise.md).

sections.title: API Keys & Account
sections.heading: Where your numbers live
sections.text:
Spend, tokens, latency percentiles, and error splits — queryable over time,
by model and by key — are on **[Usage & Metrics](usage-metrics.md)**. Partner
tooling (superkey, per-key budgets, allowlists, custom pricing) is on
**[Enterprise & Partners](enterprise.md)**.

Full endpoint reference:
[API Explorer → Customer](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer).

sections.title: Models
sections.heading: Models
sections.text:
`GET /v2/models` lists every model you can call. Each entry names the route
that serves it in `endpoint`, so a model name is all you need to build a
request. `GET /v2/models/{model}` returns one model with its route and its
list prices. Neither call needs an API key.

sections.title: Models
sections.heading: The `endpoint` object
sections.text:
| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `method`, `path` | The route to call, e.g. `POST /v2/openai/v1/chat/completions` |
| `operation_id` | The route's `operationId` in the [OpenAPI spec](api-explorer/README.md) |
| `model_in_body` | `true`: send the name as `model` in the body. `false`: the route serves this one model and names it itself, so send no `model` |
| `model_default` | The model the route uses when the body leaves `model` out; `null` when `model` is required or not taken |
| `async_default` | `true` on video routes: they answer `202` with a `task_id` unless you send `async: false` |
| `streams` | Whether the route can stream its response with `stream: true` |

`endpoint` is always present. It is `null` only when no single route can be
named for a model. `GET /v2/models/{model}` adds what to send to it and what
comes back, so one call gives you the schema and then the run:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `request_schema` | The route's request body as JSON Schema, every reference resolved |
| `request_schema_url` | Where that schema lives in the [OpenAPI document](api-explorer/README.md) |
| `request_example` | A request body that runs as-is for this model: the route's first documented example, with `model` set to this model where the body takes one. `null` when the route documents none |
| `response_schema` | What the route returns, as JSON Schema: the body on `200`, or the task's `result` when the route answers `202` (see `async_default`). `null` when `endpoint` is `null` or the route documents no response body |
| `response_schema_url` | Where the response schema lives in the OpenAPI document |

sections.title: Models
sections.heading: Get one model
sections.text:
`model` is the canonical name exactly as `GET /v2/models` lists it, slashes
included:

```bash
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/models/openai/gpt-5.4
```

```json
{
  "name": "openai/gpt-5.4",
  "display_name": "GPT-5.4",
  "tag": "text-to-text",
  "modes": ["auto", "direct"],
  "sources": ["openai"],
  "endpoint": {
    "method": "POST",
    "path": "/v2/openai/v1/chat/completions",
    "operation_id": "openai_chat_completions",
    "model_in_body": true,
    "model_default": null,
    "async_default": false,
    "streams": true
  },
  "request_schema": {"type": "object", "required": ["model", "messages"], "properties": {"model": {"type": "string"}, "messages": {"type": "array", "items": {"...": "..."}}, "...": "..."}},
  "request_schema_url": "https://relaygpu.com/v2/openapi-public.json#/components/schemas/OpenAIChatRequest",
  "request_example": {"model": "openai/gpt-5.4", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain the difference between TCP and UDP in simple terms"}], "max_tokens": 512, "temperature": 0.7},
  "response_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}, "choices": {"type": "array", "items": {"...": "..."}}, "...": "..."}},
  "response_schema_url": "https://relaygpu.com/v2/openapi-public.json#/components/schemas/OpenAIChatResponse",
  "store_output_supported": false,
  "restricted_tiers": ["guest"],
  "pricing": [
    {"mode": "direct", "model": "openai.openai/gpt-5.4", "billing_type": "per_token", "per_1m_input_tokens": 2.5, "per_1m_output_tokens": 15.0}
  ],
  "available": true,
  "status": "available"
}
```

- `modes` lists `auto` whenever the model runs in any mode (see [Modes](modes.md)).
- `restricted_tiers` names the default tiers barred from the model (see `GET /v2/tiers`).
- `pricing` carries the same rows `GET /v2/pricing` lists for the model. These
  are list prices: a custom (partner) tier may have its own contract rates,
  which are not shown here.
- `status: "retired"` means the model is no longer offered and requests for it
  are refused. `modes`, `sources` and `pricing` are then empty; `endpoint`
  still names the route that served it where one exists.
- An unknown name returns `404` with code `MODEL_NOT_FOUND` (see [Errors](errors.md)).

sections.title: Models
sections.heading: Media inputs
sections.text:
Request fields that take media by link (`image_url`, `video_url`, `audio_url`,
`reference_video_url`, and the like) accept any public `https` URL. To use a
file from your own machine, upload it with [Files](../endpoints/files.md) first
and pass the returned `url`. Some routes take source video or audio **only** as
a URL; the [Video](../endpoints/video.md#source-video-and-audio-inputs) and
[Audio](../endpoints/audio.md) pages name them.

sections.title: Modes
sections.heading: Modes
sections.text:
Every inference request runs in one **mode**. You choose it with the `mode`
field in the request **body** (not a header or query parameter). Leave it out
and it defaults to `auto`.

sections.title: Modes
sections.heading: Modes
sections.text:
| Mode | Latency | Trust | Description |
|------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `direct` | <1s | Relay-managed | Managed GPU providers |
| `opengpu` | 1-2s | Trustless | [OpenGPU Network](https://opengpu.network): permissionless, redundant computing, on-chain settlement |
| `auto` (default) | — | — | Relay picks `direct` or `opengpu` for you (below) |

sections.title: Modes
sections.heading: Usage
sections.text:
```json
{
  "model": "openai/gpt-5.4",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "mode": "direct"
}
```

- **`auto`** uses `direct` when the model is available to you there, otherwise
  `opengpu`, otherwise the request is refused with `403`. It chooses once,
  before the request runs: a request that fails in one mode is not retried in
  the other.
- **Not every model runs in both modes**, and many routes are direct-only (their
  `mode` field accepts only `auto` or `direct`). `GET /v2/models` lists the
  models per mode; asking for a mode a model does not run in returns `403`.
- **Mode availability is live data, not a promise.** `GET /v2/models` is the
  only source for which models run in `opengpu` right now; that list can be
  empty, in which case `auto` serves everything in `direct`.
- Streaming and webhooks are direct-mode only.

sections.title: Modes
sections.heading: Telling which mode served you
sections.text:
Responses have the same shape in every mode, so SDKs parse them unchanged.
Responses and task records carry a `task_id` (`direct:{uuid}` or
`opengpu:{uuid}`) and a `mode` field naming the mode that served the request.
OpenGPU tasks also carry a `task_address` (a blockchain address, verifiable on
[ogpuscan.io](https://ogpuscan.io)).

sections.title: Rate Limits
sections.heading: Rate Limits
sections.text:
Requests are limited per minute (RPM) by your tier. Each tier has three
limits: one for `direct` mode, one for `opengpu` mode, and a `global` limit
across both. A request must fit under its mode's limit and the global one.

Limits are **per customer**: all your API keys share one pool, so adding keys
does not add capacity.

sections.title: Rate Limits
sections.heading: Your limits
sections.text:
The limits are tuned over time, so read them live from `GET /v2/tiers` rather
than hard-coding them:

```bash
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/tiers -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY"
```

Each entry in `tiers` carries `rate_limits` (`direct`, `opengpu`, `global`,
in requests per minute) and `max_keys`; `current_tier` is the tier of the key
you sent (`guest` without one). Guests get the lowest limits.

Partner tiers can also cap individual keys below the tier limit; see
[API Keys & Account](keys.md).

**Need higher limits?** [Contact us](mailto:info@opengpu.network) about
enterprise options.

sections.title: Rate Limits
sections.heading: When you hit a limit
sections.text:
```
HTTP 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 60
```

```json
{"detail": "Rate limit exceeded: 16/15 RPM for direct mode (tier: basic)"}
```

The `error.code` is `RATE_LIMITED`. The message reports your current count,
the limit, which pool you hit, and your tier. Hitting the global pool reads
`Global rate limit exceeded: 21/20 RPM across all modes (tier: basic)`. The
window is one minute; wait `Retry-After` seconds before retrying.

sections.title: Usage & Metrics
sections.heading: Usage & Metrics
sections.text:
One place to answer "what did my traffic do": spend, tokens, latency, and
errors — queryable over time, grouped by model or key.

| You want | Endpoint | View | Available on |
|---|---|---|---|
| Credit balance right now | `GET /v2/customer/credits` | single number | all tiers |
| Spend & tokens per key and model | `GET /v2/customer/usage` | lifetime totals, or a daily breakdown up to 30 days | all tiers |
| Cost/token time-series to bill your own users | `GET /v2/customer/usage/timeseries` | `1m`/`1h`/`1d` buckets; group & filter by model and key | **partner tiers only** ([Enterprise & Partners](enterprise.md#per-key-cost)) |
| Latency percentiles (incl. TTFT) + success/error splits | `GET /v2/customer/metrics` | `1m`/`1h`/`1d` buckets; group by model, source, mode, key | all tiers |

Auth for all of these: your **JWT**, or on enterprise/partner accounts your
**superkey** ([keys explained](keys.md)). Regular inference keys can't read
account data. Your balance also comes with
[`GET /v2/customer/profile`](keys.md#your-profile).

sections.title: Usage & Metrics
sections.heading: Usage & cost
sections.text:
`GET /v2/customer/usage` returns **one entry per key** (secrets masked), each
broken down as nested `{mode: {source: {model: {...}}}}` objects carrying
`requests`, `credits` (the cost), `input_tokens` and `output_tokens`, plus the
key's remaining `key_budget` where one is set. `GET /v2/customer/usage/{key_id}` is
the same view for a single key.

With [prompt caching](../endpoints/chat.md#prompt-caching-anthropic), `input_tokens` counts the whole prompt: fresh input, cache reads and cache writes together. The partner time-series below also reports `cached_input_tokens` (cache reads) separately.

```bash
# All keys, lifetime totals per model
curl https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/usage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT"

# One key, daily breakdown
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/usage/{key_id}?period=7d" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT"
```

The query picks one of two mutually exclusive views:

- **No date params** → `lifetime` totals (all-time).
- **`period=7d`/`30d`**, or **`from`+`to`** (`YYYY-MM-DD`, both required) →
  `by_date` daily breakdown. Max 30 days either way, and `period` can't be
  combined with `from`/`to` (400).

Large key fleets should paginate: pass `limit` (max 1000) to page newest-first,
then pass the response's `next_cursor` back as `starting_after` while
`has_more` is true (the same cursor grammar as `GET /keys`). Omitting `limit`
returns every key in one response. Envelope:
`{ total, limit, has_more, next_cursor, keys, query }`.

There is also a **queryable** cost view for billing your own users
(`GET /v2/customer/usage/timeseries`: group and filter by model and `key_id`
over any date range). It is **available on partner (custom) tiers only** —
standard tiers get `403` and should use `GET /v2/customer/usage` above. See
[Enterprise & Partners](enterprise.md#per-key-cost).

sections.title: Usage & Metrics
sections.heading: Metrics
sections.text:
`GET /v2/customer/metrics` returns bucketed latency + reliability time-series
over your own traffic: request/success/error counts (with a user-vs-upstream
error split) and **p50/p90/p95/p99 latency**, end-to-end and upstream
separately, so you can tell "Relay overhead" from "the model was slow".
Available on **every** tier. Cost/tokens live in `/usage` (above); this
endpoint owns latency and reliability, not spend.

```bash
curl "https://relaygpu.com/v2/customer/metrics?start_time=1783000800&bucket_width=1h&group_by=model" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT"
```

sections.title: Usage & Metrics
sections.heading: Query parameters
sections.text:
| Param | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `start_time` | int (unix s) | **required**, inclusive |
| `end_time` | int (unix s) | defaults to now, exclusive; **pin it when paginating** (below) |
| `bucket_width` | `1m` \| `1h` \| `1d` | default `1d` |
| `group_by` | repeatable | `model`, `source`, `mode`, `key_id`; splits each bucket into per-value rows |
| `models` / `sources` / `modes` / `key_ids` | repeatable | filter to matching traffic |
| `limit` | int | buckets per page; default/max by width: `1d` 7/31, `1h` 24/168, `1m` 60/1440 |
| `page` | string | opaque cursor from a previous `next_page` |

sections.title: Usage & Metrics
sections.heading: Response
sections.text:
```json
{
  "object": "page",
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "bucket",
      "start_time": 1783000800,
      "end_time": 1783004400,
      "results": [
        {
          "request_count": 1240,
          "success_count": 1231,
          "error_count": 9,
          "user_error_count": 7,
          "upstream_error_count": 2,
          "unclassified_error_count": 0,
          "latency_ms":          { "p50": 812.3, "p90": 1503.1, "p95": 1902.7, "p99": 3110.0, "sample_count": 1231 },
          "provider_latency_ms": { "p50": 640.1, "p90": 1310.5, "p95": 1700.2, "p99": 2880.4, "sample_count": 1231 },
          "ttft_ms":             { "p50": 210.4, "p90": null,   "p95": null,   "p99": null,   "sample_count": 6 },
          "model": "openai/gpt-5.2"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "object": "summary",
    "start_time": 1783000800,
    "end_time": 1783087200,
    "results": [
      { "request_count": 28840, "success_count": 28610, "error_count": 230,
        "latency_ms": { "p50": 806.2, "p90": 1498.0, "p95": 1890.4, "p99": 3020.1, "sample_count": 28610 } }
    ]
  },
  "has_more": true,
  "next_page": "1"
}
```

**Fields**
- **Counts**: `request_count`, `success_count`, `error_count`, and the split: `user_error_count` (4xx-class), `upstream_error_count` (5xx / infra), `unclassified_error_count` (no mappable status). `error_count` is the three summed, so counts always reconcile. The class comes from the status of the **verdict you received** — for a streamed request that failed after its first chunk, that is the status carried by the error event that ended the stream, not the `200` the connection opened with.
- **Percentile sets**: `latency_ms` (end-to-end), `provider_latency_ms` (upstream provider call), and `ttft_ms` (time-to-first-token, **streaming only**: request receipt → first SSE chunk). All three are computed over **successful requests only** — errors are counted in the error split, never timed. Each is `{ p50, p90, p95, p99 }` in **milliseconds** plus a **`sample_count`** (how many requests fed it). A percentile is `null` when there aren't enough samples to be trustworthy, not only when the bucket is empty: `p50` needs ≥1 sample, `p90` ≥10, `p95` ≥20, `p99` ≥100. So a 6-request bucket reports `p50` but nulls `p90/p95/p99` (a "p99" over 6 requests is just the single slowest one, not a real tail). `ttft_ms` is also null wherever there's no streamed traffic. Percentiles are approximate, and `sample_count` is never above `success_count`.
- **Summary**: alongside `data`, a top-level **`summary`** object carries the **whole-range** totals: the same row shape as a bucket's `results`, but aggregated over the entire range (not per bucket, not per page), with `start_time` and `end_time` aligned to bucket edges. Use it for headline numbers without summing pages yourself. The sample floors above apply here too, but pooling the whole range usually clears a floor a thin bucket couldn't.
- **Dimension echoes**: `model` / `source` / `mode` / `key_id` appear on a row **only** when you `group_by` that dimension; grouping by `key_id` also attaches the key's **`key_name`**. An empty bucket returns one zero-filled row carrying **no** dim keys, so grouped charts don't sprout a phantom `null` series.

sections.title: Usage & Metrics
sections.heading: Pagination
sections.text:
Windows are sliced by time, `limit` buckets per page; `has_more` + `next_page` drive it (pass `next_page` back as `page`). Two rules:
- **Pin `end_time`** across pages. It defaults to `now`, so omitting it shifts the window between requests and makes `has_more`/counts drift.
- `next_page` is **opaque** (currently numeric, but don't parse it); pass it back verbatim.

Full endpoint reference:
[API Explorer → Metrics](https://docs.relaygpu.com/reference/api-explorer).

sections.title: TypeScript SDK
sections.heading: Any model: `run()` and model resolution
sections.text:
```ts
import { Relay, isAccepted } from "@relaygpu/client";

const relay = new Relay({ apiKey: process.env.RELAY_API_KEY, baseUrl: process.env.RELAY_BASE_URL });

const out = await relay.run("Qwen/qwen-image", { prompt: "a lighthouse at dusk" }); // the output body
const sub = await relay.run("KlingTeam/v3-T2V", { prompt: "waves", duration: 3 }, { wait: false });
if (isAccepted(sub)) console.log(sub.task_id); // the 202 envelope
```

The SDK ships no model table. Every call resolves the model through `relay.models.get(name)`
(`GET /v2/models/{name}`, cached 5 min per client): its route, whether `model` goes in the body, whether
the route is async by default, and its request/response schemas. A model added to Relay after this
release works through `run()` and the family helpers (`image`, `video`, `audio`) without an upgrade; the
models this release knows also get typed inputs and autocomplete.

- An unknown name throws `ModelNotFoundError` (404); a retired one throws `ModelRetiredError` (403). Both
  before anything is submitted or billed.
- `relay.models.list({ tag: "text-to-video" })` lists the catalog; `relay.models.get(name)` returns one
  model with its `request_schema`, `request_example` and `pricing`.
- `run()` returns a sync route's body, or waits for an async route and returns the task's `result`.
  `{ wait: false }` returns the `202` envelope instead.

sections.title: TypeScript SDK
sections.heading: Async tasks and `tasks.wait`
sections.text:
Video (and any call with `async: true`) answers `202` with a `task_id`. `relay.video.generate` returns that
envelope unless you pass `{ wait: true }`; `run()` and the image/audio helpers wait by default.

```ts
const task = await relay.tasks.wait(taskId, {
  timeoutMs: 20 * 60_000,                       // the default; the task keeps running past it (APITimeoutError)
  onProgress: (p) => console.log(p.status, p.elapsed_seconds),
  signal: AbortSignal.timeout(30 * 60_000),
});
```

`tasks.wait` long-polls `GET /v2/tasks/{id}?wait=30`: a 15 s task costs one or two requests, not a poll
every second. `onProgress` fires on status transitions (`queued` → `running` → `completed`) with
`elapsed_seconds`, and that is all there is: no queue position, no logs and no cancel, by design. A failed
task throws `TaskFailedError` with `code` = the task's `error_code`. Task polls need no key: the task id is
the access token. A task's result expires 1 hour after it finishes.

Workflow runs have no long-poll: `workflows.waitRun` polls the run every 1 s, backing off to 5 s (default
budget 30 min).

sections.title: TypeScript SDK
sections.heading: Idempotency and retries
sections.text:
Every async submit (`202` routes, `video.generate`, `run()` on an async route) and every workflow run is
sent with an `Idempotency-Key`: yours (`{ idempotencyKey }`) or a generated UUID. That makes the submit
safe to retry, so the SDK retries it on a network error, a timeout or a 5xx (up to 2 times, same key).
When the server recognises a key it has already accepted, it answers with the original `202` and the SDK
returns it with `replayed: true`: no second task, no second charge. The same key with a different body
throws `IdempotencyKeyReusedError` (422). Keys live 24 hours.

```ts
const a = await relay.video.generate("KlingTeam/v3-T2V", { prompt: "waves", duration: 3 }, { idempotencyKey: "order-1234" });
const b = await relay.video.generate("KlingTeam/v3-T2V", { prompt: "waves", duration: 3 }, { idempotencyKey: "order-1234" });
// b.task_id === a.task_id, b.replayed === true
```

Sync calls (an image route answering `200`, chat, TTS) carry no key and are **never retried**: a retry
would run, and bill, the request again. GETs retry on 429/503 (honouring `Retry-After`, up to 3 times) and
on other 5xx (up to 2). `retry: false` turns every retry off.

sections.title: TypeScript SDK
sections.heading: Files and implicit uploads
sections.text:
```ts
const file = await relay.files.upload(blob, { retention: "relay1d", filename: "dance.mp4" }); // { file_id, url, expires_at, … }
await relay.files.copy("https://example.com/clip.mp4", { retention: "relay7d" }); // Relay fetches it
await relay.files.get(file.file_id);
await relay.files.list({ source: "upload" });
await relay.files.delete(file.file_id); // the link goes down now; no refund
```

- Any `*_url` / `*_urls` input also takes a `Blob`, `Uint8Array`, `ArrayBuffer` or `ReadableStream`: the SDK
  uploads it first and sends the link (quickstart 3). Implicit uploads use `relay1h` unless you pass
  `{ upload: { retention: "relay1d" } }`.
- `{ inlineImages: true }` sends images of 4 MB or less as base64 instead, on routes whose schema takes it;
  larger ones are still uploaded.
- One file is at most 100 MB (`FileTooLargeError`). The media type comes from `Blob.type`, else from the
  file's first bytes.
- `relay1h` is free within a daily quota; `relay1d`, `relay7d` and `relay30d` are billed per file at upload.

sections.title: TypeScript SDK
sections.heading: How long result links live
sections.text:
Result links (`urls`, `audio_url`, …) and uploaded files expire. By default a result link lives **1 hour**
after the task finishes. To keep outputs longer, buy storage per request with `storeOutput`:

```ts
await relay.image.generate("Qwen/qwen-image", { prompt: "a lighthouse" }, { storeOutput: "relay7d" });
```

| `storeOutput` / `retention` | Lifetime | Fee |
|---|---|---|
| `provider` (default) / `relay1h` | 1 hour | free |
| `relay1d` | 1 day | per file |
| `relay7d` | 7 days | per file |
| `relay30d` | 30 days | per file |

The fees are in `(await relay.pricing.get()).media_storage`; read them there rather than hard-coding them.

sections.title: TypeScript SDK
sections.heading: Webhooks
sections.text:
Pass `webhookUrl` on an async submit (one `task.completed` or `task.failed`) or on a workflow run (one
`workflow.completed` or `workflow.failed`). Deliveries are signed with
[Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/); `relay.webhooks.verify(rawBody, headers, secret)`
checks the signature and the timestamp (±5 min) and returns the typed event, discriminated on `event`
(quickstart 4). It makes no request and needs no credential.

- Verify the **raw** body bytes, not a re-serialised `JSON.parse` result.
- Rotation: `relay.webhooks.rotateSecret()` issues a new secret and the previous one keeps working for
  24 hours. During that window pass both: `verify(raw, headers, [current, previous])`.
- On `workflow.*` events the top-level `status` is always `"completed"` (it describes the delivery). Branch
  on `event`, or on `result.status` (`completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`; a cancelled run arrives as
  `workflow.failed`).
- Delivery is at-least-once: dedupe on the `webhook-id` header.
- `relay.webhooks.secret()`, `.rotateSecret()` and `.deliveries.list()` / `.deliveries.get(taskIdOrRunId)`
  need a JWT or a partner superkey.

sections.title: TypeScript SDK
sections.heading: Errors
sections.text:
Every error extends `RelayError`. HTTP errors extend `RelayAPIError`; the HTTP status picks the class:

| Status | Class |
|---|---|
| 400 | `InvalidRequestError` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationError` |
| 402 | `InsufficientCreditsError` |
| 403 | `PermissionDeniedError` |
| 404 | `NotFoundError` |
| 409 | `ConflictError` |
| 410 | `GoneError` |
| 422 | `ValidationError` |
| 429 | `RateLimitError` |
| 500 | `RelayInternalError` |
| 502 | `ProviderError` |
| 503 | `CapacityError` |
| 504 | `UpstreamTimeoutError` |

The `error.code` then picks a subclass: `KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` throws `KeyBudgetExhaustedError`, which is an
`InsufficientCreditsError`; `CONTENT_POLICY_DECLINED` throws `ContentPolicyDeclinedError` (a
`ValidationError`). Every code in Relay's error catalog has a class. A code this release does not know falls
back to the status class and keeps `e.code`; `e.code` may also be `null`.

```ts
import { KeyBudgetExhaustedError, RateLimitError, RelayAPIError } from "@relaygpu/client";

try {
  await relay.image.generate("Qwen/qwen-image", { prompt: "a lighthouse" });
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof KeyBudgetExhaustedError) console.error("this key's budget is spent");
  else if (e instanceof RateLimitError) console.error(`retry in ${e.retryAfter}s`);
  else if (e instanceof RelayAPIError) console.error(e.status, e.code, e.requestId, e.detail);
  else throw e;
}
```

- `e.requestId` is the id to quote to support; `e.retryAfter` (seconds) is set from `Retry-After`;
  `e.detail` is the server's detail.
- `TaskFailedError`: an async task (or workflow run) ended `failed`; `e.code` is the task's `error_code`,
  `e.taskId` and `e.task` carry the rest.
- `APIConnectionError` (no HTTP answer), `APITimeoutError` (a `timeoutMs` ran out),
  `WebhookVerificationError` (a delivery failed verification).
- Branch on the class or `e.code`, never on the message, and never on `error.source` in the response body.
